NDLEA arrests South African golfer, Kenyan chef over drug trafficking
items.description: Agency intercepts 160 explosives bound for Zamfara, seizes 4.6 tonnes of cannabis in Osun By Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested a 37-year-old South African professional golfer, Grobler Henlo, and a 25-year-old Kenyan chef, Abubakar Faiza Njambi, over an alleged attempt to smuggle 50.40 kilogrammes of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, into Nigeria. The suspects were arrested at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos, following the interception of the illicit consignment. The NDLEA spokesman, Femi Babafemi, said the golfer’s arrest came exactly one month before the agency intercepted an American professional basketball player, Greene Da’monte Khiree, at the same airport on November 11, 2026, over the importation of 33.95 kilogrammes of the same psychoactive substance. According to the agency, Henlo arrived in Lagos from South Africa aboard a South African Airways flight on October 11 and was intercepted at the Terminal 2 arrival hall. A search of two travelling boxes in his possession reportedly led to the discovery of 46 parcels of Loud weighing 50.40 kilogrammes. Investigations revealed that although the boxes were in Henlo’s possession, they bore the luggage tags of his alleged accomplice, Njambi, who had collected two other boxes bearing his tags from the airport conveyor belt before leaving the airport. The agency said the exchange of luggage tags was a deliberate attempt by the syndicate to frustrate the identification of ownership and enable each courier to deny the boxes bearing their respective names if intercepted. During preliminary questioning, Henlo reportedly disclosed that he was recruited by a South African associate identified as Shanel, who linked him with other members of the syndicate whom he had never met physically. He said a driver picked him up from his home in South Africa, handed him four travelling boxes and took him to the airport, where he was instructed to meet Njambi and exchange luggage tags. The golfer reportedly said he was promised 5,000 South African rand upon successful delivery of the consignment. Further examination revealed that tracking devices had been installed in the travelling boxes and on his mobile phone, a development the agency said was similar to what was discovered in the bags abandoned by the American basketball player a month later. The NDLEA said the discovery showed how closely the cartels monitored their couriers and consignments. It added that the passport biodata page of Njambi, recovered from Henlo’s phone, was used to profile her and place her on the agency’s watchlist. She was subsequently arrested at the departure boarding gate of the Lagos airport on October 15 while attempting to board a South African Airways flight to Kenya. The 25-year-old private chef reportedly told investigators that she was recruited through a man who was introduced to her by a friend in Kenya and promised $8,000 upon successful delivery of the consignment. She said she travelled from Kenya to South Africa on October 4, stayed in a hotel for about a week and met Henlo at the airport on October 11, where he handed her two of the four boxes before they checked them in under their respective luggage tags. On arrival in Lagos, she allegedly collected the two boxes bearing the golfer’s tags before a driver took her to a hotel in the Lekki area. The claim tag for the two boxes bearing her name, which she reportedly abandoned at the airport, was recovered from her hand luggage. Both suspects subsequently identified each other during an identification parade. Other seizures, arrests In a separate operation at the import shed of the Lagos airport on November 13, NDLEA operatives intercepted a consolidated consignment that arrived from the United Kingdom aboard an Allied Air flight. The agency said a freight agent, Sobowale Oladayo, was arrested when he presented himself to clear the shipment. A search of the consignment led to the recovery of 10 parcels of synthetic cannabinoid weighing 10.10 kilogrammes, 27 packs of marshmallow weighing 318.80 kilogrammes and precursor chemicals comprising 11 containers of N,N-Dimethylformamide (DMF) weighing 18.90 kilogrammes, 10 containers of 5-Bromo-1-Pentane weighing 8.05 kilogrammes and seven containers of Potassium Carbonate weighing 7.60 kilogrammes. The total gross weight of the recovered items was 363.45 kilogrammes. In a follow-up operation on November 14, the agency arrested the consignee, identified as Kareem Issa, 35, also known as Ola, when he arrived to collect the shipment at a logistics company’s premises in a grey Lexus 460 SUV, accompanied by two other persons. The NDLEA said Issa, a plumber by profession who lives on Lagos Island, allegedly presented himself as a senior security personnel. Investigations reportedly showed that he routinely activated the siren fitted to his vehicle whenever he visited the logistics company to collect consignments, allegedly to portray himself as a security operative and avoid attention. In Kaduna State, operatives on patrol along the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway at Jere on November 17 arrested a 35-year-old man, Lawali Muhammad, with 160 pieces of explosives allegedly being transported to Zamfara State. The intended recipient, identified as Aliyu Mohammed, 30, was subsequently arrested in a follow-up operation in Gusau on the same day. Also arrested along the Jere axis were two suspects, Yusuf Magaji and Buhari Yusuf, 32, with 6,900 tablets of tramadol 225mg, 20,000 tablets of diazepam and 25,000 tablets of Exol-5. Similarly, operatives along the Zaria-Kano Expressway at Gwargwaje, Zaria, recovered 627,500 capsules of tramadol weighing 21.50 kilogrammes from a Hummer bus whose driver reportedly abandoned the vehicle and fled upon sighting the officers. In Ogun State, a woman, Esther Ogundipe, was arrested on November 19 during a raid on a drug joint at Eleweran, Abeokuta, with two locally made firearms and five live cartridges. Two days earlier, two other female suspects, Balikis Ogunbiyi and Omobola Ajani, were arrested during a raid in Ilaro with 7.4 grammes of cocaine, 638 grammes of cannabis and 5.9 grammes of methamphetamine. In Osun State, a 43-year-old man, Francis Oduke, was arrested along the Ikire-Ibadan Expressway with 359 bags of skunk weighing 4,627.7 kilogrammes, concealed beneath a load of granite in a truck. In neighbouring Ondo State, operatives intercepted a truck conveying 93 bags of cannabis weighing 1,045 kilogrammes to Kano State along the Zango-Ado Expressway, Akure, on November 16. The agency said the interception followed intelligence gathering and surveillance of the vehicle, which was loaded in Ogbese town. Four suspects, Adamu Yerima, 19; Mohammed Mohammed, 19; Nura Mohammed, 25; and Usman Mohammed, were arrested in connection with the seizure. In Edo State, a 48-year-old man, Emmanuel Eze, was arrested on November 20 with 11 and a half bags of cannabis weighing 156 kilogrammes at Aduwawa community, Benin City. In Katsina State, operatives arrested a 39-year-old man, Abbas Bello, in the Gafai area on November 17 with 148 blocks of cannabis weighing 72 kilogrammes concealed in the boot of his white Honda Accord car. In Abia State, operatives on November 18 raided a shop belonging to a 25-year-old woman, Oluebube Innocent, at Amankwa Street, Obingwa Local Government Area, recovering two kilogrammes of cannabis concealed in a hole dug into the shop’s floor and covered with ceramic tiles. The tiles were removed to recover the substance. In Rivers State, a 46-year-old physically challenged man, Peter Sunday, was arrested with 300 grammes of cannabis during a raid in Eneka on November 17. NDLEA intensifies anti-drug campaign Meanwhile, the agency said its commands and formations across the country sustained their War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) sensitisation activities in schools, worship centres, workplaces and communities during the week. The activities included enlightenment lectures for students and staff of Local Government Primary School, Ebute Ikorodu, Lagos; Government Girls Unity College, Birnin Kebbi; and Community Secondary School, Usa, Enugu Ezike. The Ondo State Command also paid a WADA advocacy visit to the Deji of Akure Kingdom, Oba Aladetoyinbo Ogunlade Adelusi, Odundun II. The Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of NDLEA, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), commended officers and men of the agency’s commands in Lagos, Kaduna, Ogun, Osun, Ondo, Edo, Katsina, Abia and Rivers states for the arrests and seizures. Marwa said the arrests of the South African golfer and the Kenyan chef, coming within the same period as that of the American basketball player, indicated that international drug cartels were changing the profiles of their couriers but retaining their methods. “The two cases show a trend in which international drug cartels now recruit sportsmen and other professionals as couriers, in the hope that their profiles will shield them from scrutiny. “The NDLEA has a clear message for such syndicates: no profession, passport or travel class will provide cover for drug trafficking through Nigeria’s ports of entry,” he warned. He urged officers at all ports of entry to remain vigilant and professional, while charging commands across the country to sustain efforts at reducing both drug supply and demand. He particularly called for intensified WADA sensitisation campaigns in schools, workplaces, worship centres and communities. The post NDLEA arrests South African golfer, Kenyan chef over drug trafficking appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Veteran journalist Husain Naqi passes away in Lahore
items.description: LAHORE: Veteran journalist and human rights activist Husain Naqi passed away in Lahore on Sunday. He was a former editor of The News and had also been associated with the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP). HRCP official Muhammad Ilyas told Dawn that Naqi died of a cardiac arrest. “He attended a book launch ceremony at the HRCP the previous day. Later, he suffered a heart attack around 6pm on Saturday. He was admitted to a private hospital where he died early in the morning, around 5 am,” Ilyas said, adding that he had left behind three sons. Naqi was buried in Model Town Extension in Lahore. Meanwhile, condolences over his passing continued to pour in. President Asif Ali Zardari extended his condolences to the bereaved family, expressing “deep sorrow”, a statement issued by the Presidency said. The president paid tribute to Naqi’s “services to journalism, freedom of expression and human rights”, the statement said. It further quoted the president as saying: “Husain Naqi played a prominent role in promoting journalism and democratic values. His contributions will always be remembered.” The HRCP also released a statement, saying it “deeply mourns” Naqi’s passing. “Over a career spanning more than 70 years, from student leader to newspaper editor to treasurer of HRCP, neither multiple incarcerations nor vindictive acts by the authorities ever weakened his resolve to speak truth to power. Naqi sahib served HRCP in different capacities for three decades and was an active council member at the time of his passing. One of the strongest voices for people’s rights and democracy in Pakistan has gone silent,” the statement said. PPP Senator Sherry Rehman posted on X that she was “truly grieved to hear about the sad demise of the veteran journalist and rights campaigner, the iconic Husain Naqi”. “His passing signals the end of an era. Naqi sahib always spoke unflinching truth to power. Many of us cub journalists learnt at his desk, walked in rallies under his leadership. He led so many groups and networks in the hardest days of dictatorship. “We often called him the rebel angel of our times, yet he never stoked anger. He sought the right to dissent with respect. He will be missed. May his soul rest in peace and power,” she said. PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja began his codolence on X by stating: “Alas! Naqi sahib is no longer among us.” He said his acquaintance and admiration for Naqi spanned decades. Naming I.A. Rehman, Asma Jahangir and Amin Mughal along with Naqi, Raja said, “The most precious gems who dreamed of and championed the dignity of human beings and the rising of voices of the poor in Pakistan are leaving us. “Their dreams have yet to be realised. Their dreams are the dreams of 250 million people.” Journalist Absa Komal said Naqi spent his entire life advocating for freedom of speech. “I met him a few months ago at a conference in Karachi, and he still had the same spirit and commitment to the cause. A remarkable life,” she added. Journalist Raza Rumi was more succinct in his message that said: “Rest in peace Naqi sahib.” Who was Husain Naqi? Naqi was born in Lucknow, India before the Independence in 1947. In his autobiography Mujh Se Jo Ho Saka , Naqi said he was perhaps born a year before his officially recorded birthdate in 1936. His great-grandfather had moved to Lucknow from a village in what is now Haryana, in the then-undivided Punjab. It was a well-heeled and well-educated family that flourished in Lucknow over the next few generations. However, Naqi subtly confronted the conservatism of his traditional family from a very young age. Outside, he was not subtle. He began his student activism in secondary school and started taking on the minor establishments of power at a fairly young age. After early schooling and college education in Lucknow, Naqi moved to Karachi in the 1950s, where he developed into a student leader. As a student in Karachi, Naqi played a key role in several demonstrations and protests. During the 1956 Suez Canal crisis when Egypt was attacked by Israel, France and Britain, Naqi was part of the executive committee of the National Students Federation (NSF). At the time, the NSF organised a march to the British High Commission in Karachi to protest against the attack and was faced with police batons and tear gas. As president of Karachi University’s student union, Naqi made a deal with the university’s vice-chancellor for Naqi to be rusticated for three years instead of three Baloch students who had been rusticated in response to an incident at the hostel. Naqi’s activism during his student days was not just centred around protests but also had to do with improving conditions in the institution. He fought for adding a new campus with better facilities, providing safe transport for girls and ensuring that exams were held on time and not postponed. He was a strong advocate for student unions. In an interview published in 2011, he said, “it was the banning of student unions that destroyed campus peace. In our time, student unions were a positive influence. We organised cultural activities. We tolerated diversity. Representatives with various political leanings were able to work together despite their ideological differences”. After a few turbulent years in Karachi, Naqi permanently settled down in Lahore. As a journalist, Naqi found his first mentor in Javed Bokhari, with whom he worked for a couple of years. “In those days I used to literally live at the PPI office,” he had said of the time. He ended up working as the bureau chief of PPI . However, he eventually had to leave the position following a reporting incident in which he refused to accept a false news of desecration of the Holy Quran. Nonetheless, he continued to write for various newspapers, including the Viewpoint , Holiday , Outlook , Frontier Post , Frontier Guardian , Daily Star , Punjab Times and Punjab Punch . Naqi consistently campaigned for the preservation and promotion of the Punjabi language in Pakistan, starting the first-ever daily newspaper in the Punjabi language — Sajjan . Naqi had also been imprisoned a couple of times because of his outspokenness. In the 2011 interview, he recalled those instances with a sense of humour. “I was lucky to invariably have someone favourably disposed towards me at the jail premises, who made sure that I was not mistreated.”

items.title: Journalisme africain : Dakar au cœur du débat sur le financement des médias indépendants
items.description: La capitale sénégalaise accueille, les 23 et 24 novembre 2026, la Conférence des jeunes journalistes africains. Organisée par la Convention des jeunes reporters du Sénégal (CJRS), en partenariat avec la Fondation Konrad Adenauer, cette rencontre entend explorer les modèles économiques susceptibles de garantir la viabilité des entreprises de presse sans compromettre leur indépendance éditoriale. Le journalisme africain est confronté à un défi de taille : trouver les moyens de financer durablement la production de l’information sans sacrifier sa liberté. C’est autour de cette problématique que de jeunes professionnels des médias, venus de plusieurs pays du continent, se retrouveront à Dakar, les 23 et 24 novembre 2026, à l’occasion de la Conférence des jeunes journalistes africains, placée sous le thème : « Quel modèle économique pour un journalisme indépendant ? ». À l’initiative de la Convention des jeunes reporters du Sénégal (CJRS), en partenariat avec la Fondation Konrad Adenauer, cette rencontre intervient dans un contexte marqué par les difficultés économiques des entreprises de presse. Baisse des recettes publicitaires, fragilité des modèles traditionnels, concurrence des plateformes numériques et évolution des habitudes de consommation de l’information : les médias africains doivent composer avec des contraintes qui fragilisent leur équilibre financier et, parfois, leur capacité à remplir leur mission. Pendant deux jours, les participants sont appelés à confronter leurs expériences et à examiner les pistes susceptibles de répondre à ces interrogations. La réflexion portera notamment sur la recherche de modèles économiques plus résilients, capables de prendre en compte les nouvelles réalités du marché médiatique et les opportunités offertes par le numérique. La conférence se veut également un espace de partage et de réseautage entre jeunes journalistes africains. En réunissant des professionnels issus de différents environnements médiatiques, elle ambitionne de favoriser les échanges de pratiques, de faire émerger des initiatives communes et de renforcer les dynamiques de coopération à l’échelle continentale. À travers cette initiative, la CJRS entend contribuer à la réflexion sur l'avenir des médias africains, tout en donnant à la jeune génération les moyens de mieux appréhender les transformations de son métier. A.N

items.title: Kwame Dzokoto of Edziban fame to be buried on February 20, 2027, in Sekondi
items.description: Media personality and politician Seth Kwame Dzokoto, popularly known as Edziban, will be buried on February 20, 2027, in Sekondi in the Western Region. The funeral arrangements were announced by his family during his one-week observation at St Matthew Catholic Church in Tarkwa. The funeral activities will run from February 19 to 21, 2027, beginning with the laying in state of his body at the forecourt of the parish hall in Tarkwa on February 19. A memorial service will be held at St Matthew Catholic Church on February 20, after which his body will be transported to Sekondi for burial at the Ketan District Cemetery. A thanksgiving service will follow at the same church on Sunday, February 21. The one-week observation attracted clergy, traditional leaders, media personalities, businesspeople, politicians from the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and the New Patriotic Party (NPP), as well as family members and friends. Speaking at the gathering, the Parish Priest of St Matthew Catholic Church, Father Michael Owusu, described the late Dzokoto as a source of national pride whose contributions to Ghana would be remembered. He recalled how Dzokoto used humour on television to entertain viewers and help many Ghanaians relieve stress. Father Owusu urged Ghanaians to remain committed to their respective professions and make meaningful contributions to their families, communities and the country. He also prayed for the bereaved family. Kwame Dzokoto, who was also known as Efiewura Kwame Dzokoto, died on Thursday, October 22, 2026, aged 51.

items.title: ‘I’ve not been served’ – Jimmy Odukoya speaks on court injunction amid church crisis
items.description: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya has said he has not been formally served with the court injunction restraining him from presenting himself as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos. Odukoya made this known on Sunday while addressing the congregation during the church’s service, saying he had only heard about the injunction but had yet to receive the court order. “I heard that there was an injunction against me. I heard. I’ve not seen it. But I heard. But I’ve not been served. So, legally, I’ve not been served,” he said. His remarks came shortly after the founder of The Redeemed Evangelical Mission, Bishop Mike Okonkwo, made a surprise appearance at the service and urged members not to take sides in the leadership dispute involving Odukoya and his sister, Tolu. Thanking members for their continued support amid the controversy, Jimmy Odukoya said he appreciated their decision to attend the service despite the ongoing crisis. “In spite of everything, you are still here,” he told the congregation. He also reaffirmed his commitment to the church and its members, saying, “There is no Fountain without you. You are Fountain of Life. And as long as you are with me, I will continue to speak for you. I will continue to stand with you.” Describing the service as the quickest, Odukoya joked that Okonkwo had already delivered the sermon, leaving him with little to add. “Bishop has preached already. There is nothing to preach again,” he said, adding that he would finish speaking on time. He subsequently asked the congregation if they wanted another dance, to which members reportedly responded in the affirmative. Earlier, Okonkwo told the congregation that he was prompted by the Holy Spirit to visit the church and bless its members amid the leadership crisis. “I have not slept since 1.30 am. The Holy Spirit said to me, son, go to the Fountain and bless them. That’s why I am here,” he said. On Friday, Odukoya approached the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his reported removal as senior pastor and questioning the legality of decisions allegedly taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees. The suit, instituted alongside the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, named his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church leaders as respondents. They include Pastors Rotimi Okpaise, Tobi Enuha, Gbenga Onabanjo, Fred Ohiani and Akin Osinbajo, as well as Biodun Balogun and Biodun Awosika. Odukoya is challenging the validity of meetings held by some trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions allegedly reached at those meetings. He is also asking the court to determine whether the trustees could remove him as senior pastor without following the procedures stipulated in the church’s constitution. The dispute became public on November 17 when a group identifying itself as members of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that Odukoya was no longer recognised as senior pastor, with immediate effect. The group reportedly cited a review of the church’s constitution and succession instructions allegedly left by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, who died in August 2023. The trustees subsequently named Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader pending consultations and the establishment of a substantive leadership structure. However, the church rejected the announcement, insisting that Jimmy Odukoya remained its duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the Board of Trustees. The disagreement took another turn on November 18 when the Lagos State High Court granted interim orders restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the church’s senior pastor and spiritual head. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin also restrained him from interfering with or disrupting the church’s governance and administration. The orders were granted ex parte, meaning they were made before Odukoya had an opportunity to respond to the application. The court, however, preserved his right to challenge the orders. Meanwhile, the church postponed its 2026 Thanksgiving Service, which was scheduled for November 22, but announced that its regular Sunday worship service would hold at 9am. The church also dismissed reports that its premises had been sealed, assuring members that services would continue. The matter is expected to return to court on December 1. Vanguard News The post ‘I’ve not been served’ – Jimmy Odukoya speaks on court injunction amid church crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le président Bassirou Diomaye Faye préside la deuxième randonnée pédestre des « Jambaars »
items.description: Trois jours après la célébration de la 25e édition de la Journée des Forces armées, le Président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, retrouve les hommes et les femmes en uniforme, ce dimanche 22 novembre 2026, à la caserne Samba Diéry Diallo. Cette randonnée pédestre annuelle, dont la première édition s'est tenue en novembre 2025, vise à renforcer la cohésion au sein de l'institution militaire et à consolider les liens entre l'Armée et la Nation. Les chaussures de marche prennent le relais des rangers. Le Président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, Chef suprême des Armées, préside, ce dimanche 22 novembre 2026, la randonnée pédestre annuelle du ministère des Forces armées, à la caserne Samba Diéry Diallo. Cette activité sportive, désormais inscrite dans l'agenda républicain, constitue un moment de rassemblement pour les différentes composantes des Forces armées, autour des valeurs de solidarité, de discipline et de fraternité d'armes. Cette deuxième édition intervient dans le prolongement de la célébration de la Journée des Forces armées, organisée le jeudi 19 novembre 2026 au quartier Dial Diop, siège de l'État-major général des Armées. Présidée par le chef de l'Etat Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, cette 25e édition était placée sous le thème : « Les Forces armées, vecteurs de l'intégration sous-régionale et de la sécurité collective ». La cérémonie avait réuni des autorités gouvernementales et diplomatiques, des responsables civils et militaires, ainsi que des membres du Comité des chefs d'état-major des Armées de la Communauté économique des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (CEDEAO). À travers cette thématique, le Sénégal entendait mettre en lumière la nécessité d'une coopération militaire renforcée face aux défis sécuritaires qui dépassent les frontières nationales. Dans son adresse, le Chef de l'État avait notamment plaidé pour une meilleure coordination entre les armées ouest-africaines, le partage du renseignement et la multiplication des exercices militaires conjoints. Il avait également insisté sur le renforcement de l'autonomie stratégique régionale et continentale. La célébration avait été marquée par le baptême de deux promotions militaires : la 58e promotion de l'École militaire de santé, désormais baptisée médecin-colonel Mady Oury Sylla, et la 45e promotion de l'École nationale des officiers d'active, qui porte le nom du capitaine André Senghor. Quatre militaires et gendarmes blessés en opérations avaient également reçu des médailles. Pour rappel, la Journée des Forces armées commémore la remise, le 10 novembre 1960, du drapeau du premier Régiment des tirailleurs sénégalais au premier bataillon d'infanterie. Habituellement célébrée le 10 novembre, elle a été exceptionnellement décalée au 19 novembre cette année, en raison de l'organisation des Jeux olympiques de la Jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. A.N

items.title: Accord de paix en Ukraine : Trump fixe comme date butoir début janvier et accentue la pression sur Kiev
items.description: L'administration du president americain Donald Trump a fait savoir aux responsables europeens et ukrainiens qu'elle souhaitait la conclusion d'un accord de paix entre Kiev et Moscou d'ici debut janvier, a rapporte le 20 novembre le Financial Times en citant des sources. Selon le journal americain, la Maison Blanche entend accelerer le processus de paix avant que les democrates ne prennent le controle du Congres americain. Un responsable europeen a notamment declare, a l'issue d'une rencontre avec les negociateurs de Donald Trump pour l'Ukraine Jared Kushner et Steve Witkoff, que « les Americains exercent une forte pression » et qu'« il y a des craintes » que la conclusion d'un accord ne necessite de « tres nombreuses concessions » de la part de l'Ukraine. Un autre responsable a indique au journal que « les Americains ont hâte ». Le Financial Times a egalement souligne que les responsables americains cherchaient a regler simultanement les differends territoriaux et les questions plus larges de securite europeenne. Le journal a rappele que Jared Kushner et Steve Witkoff avaient tenu ces derniers jours une serie de reunions avec des responsables russes, ukrainiens et europeens a Moscou, Dublin et Berlin. Selon les interlocuteurs du Financial Times , les negociateurs americains ont insiste sur la necessite d'un reglement urgent de la question. Restrictions de Starshield et des missiles Patriot : les etats-Unis font pression sur Kiev La date butoir fixee par Washington, debut janvier, a renforce les craintes de Kiev selon lesquelles la partie ukrainienne pourrait etre contrainte d'« accepter les conditions de Moscou » avant l'arrivee des democrates au Congres. Par ailleurs, les responsables ukrainiens ont interprete les recentes restrictions de vitesse imposees a Starshield, la version militaire du systeme de communication par satellite Starlink de SpaceX, ainsi que les retards observes ces derniers mois dans la livraison des missiles intercepteurs Patriot, comme s'inscrivant dans le cadre des efforts americains visant a affaiblir la position de Kiev et a intensifier la pression afin d'obtenir des concessions de la part de la Russie, a note le journal. Des representants americains ont egalement laisse entendre que Donald Trump aborderait la question de la fin du conflit avec les dirigeants europeens lors du sommet du G20, qu'il accueillera a Miami en decembre, a indique le Financial Times . Toutefois, un haut responsable francais a declare qu'il n'y aurait pas de negociations avec les Europeens sur l'Ukraine lors de ce sommet, car Kiev « n'a pas recu d'invitation ». Le president russe Vladimir Poutine a ete invite a cette reunion, mais n'a pas encore decide s'il y participerait. Le reglement pacifique depend de Kiev Lors du sommet de la Cooperation economique Asie-Pacifique (APEC) , qui s'est tenu dans la ville chinoise de Shenzhen les 18 et 19 novembre, le chef de l'etat russe a souligne que l'Ukraine devait accepter les compromis proposes par les etats-Unis avant le sommet americano-russe a Anchorage, en Alaska, en août 2025, si elle souhaite mettre fin au conflit. Selon le president russe, Moscou a deja accepte ces propositions, et il appartient desormais a Kiev d'en faire de meme. Le dirigeant russe a egalement souligne que Donald Trump et Xi Jinping avaient mis en avant l'interet des etats-Unis, de la Chine et de la communaute internationale pour le reglement du conflit ukrainien. Il a confirme que la Russie ne souhaitait pas poursuivre les hostilites, tout en precisant que leur cessation dependait desormais de Kiev. En outre, Vladimir Poutine a propose d'envoyer a Moscou des representants des pays europeens afin qu'ils precisent leurs positions dans le cadre d'echanges diplomatiques. Le chef de l'etat russe a neanmoins critique la militarisation de l'UE, la qualifiant de defi majeur pour la Russie. Selon lui, les dirigeants europeens compromettent les perspectives de paix en Ukraine en proposant de deployer des troupes sur le territoire ukrainien. La question du deploiement d'un contingent militaire en Ukraine est revenue sur le devant de la scene suite aux recents appels du president francais Emmanuel Macron en faveur de la reprise des discussions sur l'adhesion de Kiev a l'OTAN , en raison de la position pretendument « maximaliste » de la Russie. Or, cette position reste inacceptable pour Moscou depuis de nombreuses annees. Toujours lors du sommet de l'APEC, le president russe a rappele que l'Ukraine avait initialement inscrit le principe de neutralite dans sa declaration d'independance, avant de se tourner vers l'Alliance.

items.title: Intrants de drones : les exportations marocaines grimpent de 60 %
items.description: Le Transition Report 2026-27 de la BERD relève une envolée de 60 % des exportations marocaines de biens destinés à la fabrication de drones, sans en révéler ni le volume ni la composition. Dans son chapitre sur l'économie des dépenses de défense, le Transition Report 2026-27 de la Banque européenne pour la reconstruction et le développement (BERD), publié mardi 17 novembre, examine le marché des drones sous deux angles : celui des appareils finis et celui des composants qui servent à les produire. C'est dans ce second volet, à la page 62, que le royaume apparaît. Ses ventes à l'étranger de produits classés comme intrants ont été multipliées par 1,6 entre la moyenne des années 2019 à 2021 et l'année 2024, soit une hausse de 60 %. Cette progression concerne des biens situés en amont de l'assemblage des appareils, et non les drones eux-mêmes. Le document place cette performance dans un groupe de pays. La Slovénie et la Slovaquie affichent exactement la même évolution, la Bulgarie a doublé ses envois, et la Serbie domine le tableau avec une progression de 220 %, ses exportations ayant été multipliées par 3,2. Ces coefficients disent la vitesse, pas l'ampleur : le passage ne publie aucune valeur en dollars, si bien qu'on ignore si le Maroc exporte davantage ou moins que ses voisins du classement. Un même taux de croissance peut partir de bases très éloignées. Pour établir ce résultat, la BERD s'appuie sur BACI, la base de commerce international du Centre d'études prospectives et d'informations internationales (CEPII), à laquelle renvoie la note 41 du rapport. Alimentée par Comtrade, la base des Nations unies, elle rapproche les déclarations des pays vendeurs de celles des pays acheteurs, avec des valeurs en milliers de dollars, des quantités en tonnes et des catégories douanières à six chiffres. Le CEPII ajuste notamment les écarts liés au fret et à l'assurance avant de concilier les deux versions. Les échanges marocains analysés couvrent la période allant jusqu'en 2024. Le taux de 60 % mesure l'évolution de la valeur des exportations. Il ne renseigne pas sur le nombre de pièces expédiées, faute de données publiées sur les tonnages et sur les prix. Il n'isole pas non plus la part de valeur créée sur le sol marocain, la valeur d'une exportation et l'apport de l'industrie locale étant deux grandeurs distinctes. Pour les aéronefs complets, la BERD change de grille. Son graphique 2.20 s'appuie sur la position 8806 du Système harmonisé de 2022, celle des aéronefs sans pilote, et répartit les appareils en trois classes selon leur masse maximale au décollage. Cette nomenclature ne recoupe pas la liste de produits retenue pour les intrants. Le découpage par poids renseigne en outre assez peu sur l'identité de l'utilisateur final. Dans cette catégorie, la Chine pèse 64,8 % des exportations mondiales de petits drones et 36,9 % de celles des modèles intermédiaires. La Turquie détient 41,2 % du marché des grands appareils, devant les États-Unis (20,7 %). The post Intrants de drones : les exportations marocaines grimpent de 60 % appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: La parole se libère en public
items.description: Bégaiement, trac, trou noir lors d’un discours : voilà quelques-unes des lacunes que les formateurs en prise de parole en public, en art oratoire ou en développement personnel essaient de corriger chez ceux qui en sentent le besoin. Ces derniers, au sortir de séances privées ou en groupe, reversent un tribut à leurs encadreurs, des hommes et des femmes qui vivent de ce métier. Quatre hommes et une femme forment un cercle. Main dans la main, ils créent des combinaisons de déplacement à tour de rôle et essaient de les suivre sans se tromper. « Gauche, gauche, droite », la première combinaison à être donnée. Chacun, ses doigts dans la paume de son voisin, se décale de deux pas vers la gauche, d’un autre vers la droite. Puis, un autre invente une nouvelle combinaison que le reste du groupe suit naturellement. Ils poursuivent le rythme jusqu’à ce que le coach en prise de parole en public et en art oratoire, Malick Souleymane Kouyaté, arrête la séance. C’est dans cette ambiance aussi décontractée que ludique que se déroulent les apprentissages dans une école de formation en prise de parole en public et en art oratoire, de la place. D’un applaudissement, coach Kouyaté, le front perlé de sueur malgré le souffle frisquet du climatiseur, explique que cela permet de libérer les corps. « Il faut d’abord préparer le corps avant de s’attaquer à la voix. Car c’est le corps qui supporte la voix », enseigne-t-il, un léger dégradé ceignant sa tête de vingtenaire. Installé dans une salle où le mobilier semble être abhorré, le coach Kouyaté et ses apprentis, pieds nus ou en chaussettes, enchaînent, debout ou assis à même d’une moquette grise, plusieurs autres ateliers. C’est ainsi que des encouragements sont formulés pour pousser chacun à sortir de sa bulle. Ababacar Ba, élève en classe de première, est l’un des douze membres de cette nouvelle cohorte dont beaucoup, venus plus tôt, ne sont plus là. Inscrit par sa grande sœur, ce jeune homme, regard fuyant et mains dans les poches, avoue avoir peur d’engager des discussions. « C’est pour cela que ma sœur a senti le besoin de m’inscrire ici », poursuit-il, d’un trait. Des tarifs de 60.000 à 500.000 FCfa Cette formation d’un mois en prise de parole en public, la sœur de Ababacar l’a payée à 60.000 FCfa, révèle le coach Kouyaté, assis en tailleur sur la moquette. Le prix des sessions n’est pas uniforme. « Pour les formations en groupe, le tarif va de 60.000 à 500.000 FCfa », révèle le coach Kouyaté, plongé dans son large boubou gris. Ce gap entre les tarifs est dû, entre autres, dans cette école sise à Sacré-Cœur, à la durée des formations, selon Malick Souleymane Kouyaté. Le profil des apprentis influence aussi le coût des formations. Jean Paul Ndour, coach en art oratoire et en transformation du capital humain -une appellation plus correcte de « développement personnel » selon lui-, propose des tarifs en fonction du profil. Trouvé à la Place de l’Indépendance de Dakar, où il traverse à grandes enjambées une des larges routes goudronnées qui étreignent le lieu, ce journaliste et présentateur télé monte, son sac en cuir sur le dos, les marches poussiéreuses de la Chambre de Commerce. Un coup de mouchoir passé sur quelques carreaux blancs, il s’installe, genoux pliés. Jean Paul explique avec fluidité : « Pour les étudiants, c’est 10.000 FCfa l’heure. Quant aux professionnels, en fonction du profil et des prérequis, les tarifs peuvent varier entre 15.000, 20.000 jusqu’à 100.000 FCfa pour une heure de formation ». Son tee-shirt blanc toujours agrippé à son corps malgré le vent assez fort dans cette allée, coach Ndour, poursuit : « Je ne peux pas appliquer le tarif d’un étudiant à un ministre de la République ». Cette dernière affirmation illustre de la diversité des profils ayant recours aux services des formateurs en art oratoire, prise de parole en public ou en développement personnel. De l’étudiant au député et au maire, en passant par l’avocat et le juge, les coachs côtoient divers secteurs. Ce qui les pousse à adapter la formation, affirme Ibrahima Khaliloulah Mbaye, coach en art oratoire et en développement personnel dans une autre école. Selon ce passionné d’art oratoire depuis le lycée, tout est fait pour adapter la formation aux besoins professionnels de l’apprenti. Derrière son écran, il confie que c’est pour cela que les séances individuelles sont plus coûteuses dans leur académie. Celles qui se font en groupe varient entre 45.000 FCfa et plus de 400.000 FCfa, affirme Mouhamed Mballo, collègue de coach Mbaye, dont seul le buste apparaît sur l’écran. Dans la salle des cours de pratique de l’académie de Sacré-Cœur, le climatiseur continue, dans une surdité absolue, à souffler son air frais. À 13 heures passées de quelques minutes, le coach Malick Souleymane Kouyaté fait ses au revoir à ses apprentis. Assiatou Diallo, seule femme présente à cette heure, est l’une d’eux. Étudiante en première année de thèse, elle suit une formation en prise de parole en public afin d’avoir un contrôle sur son bégaiement. Assise sur l’une des rares chaises traînant dans cette salle, la dame affirme être prête à payer ce qu’il faut. « La communication, c’est la base. Quand tu sais bien parler, tu as tout ; donc le prix de la formation importe peu », justifie-t-elle, son foulard noir, légèrement au-dessus de son front. Un antidote Le règlement des frais de formation permet de payer le loyer des locaux de l’école et ses employés. Safiatou Ndiaye, chargé d’orientation et coach, explique que chaque employé est rémunéré en fonction de ses services. « Après avoir fait les comptes, on s’acquitte du loyer. Puis, chacun reçoit une somme à la hauteur des prestations qu’il a fournies durant le mois », confie-t-elle, le regard fixe, toisant son piercing. L’académie compte actuellement trois cohortes de douze apprentis chacune. À ces apprentis s’ajoutent ceux qui subissent des formations privées. Toutes ces personnes s’acquittent d’une inscription, payée d’un coup ou par tranche selon le coach Kouyaté. Un grand sourire affiché, il voit ainsi en la formation en prise de parole en public et en art oratoire, un métier qui nourrit son homme. Une déclaration que Safiatou Ndiaye confirme sans hésitation. « On rend vraiment grâce à Dieu », lâche-t-elle, le sourire aux lèvres. Le métier de coach en art oratoire fait des heureux jusqu’aux marches de la Chambre de Commerce. Toujours assis, Jean Paul Ndour échange, à vive voix, quelques plaisanteries avec un homme qui a reconnu le présentateur télé. Ses mains, escortant toujours sa parole, l’homme confie bien s’en sortir. « Ces formations permettent de gérer la location, la famille, les besoins », partage-t-il, le regard soutenu. Ce qui en fait des métiers d’avenir selon les coachs Mouhamed Mballo et Ibrahima Khaliloulah Mbaye, toujours « coincés » dans leur écran. Coach Mbaye, une barbe montante presque aux joues, affirme : « La demande a précédé l’offre. On nous sollicitait pour des conseils avant même qu’on se lance dans la formation ». La demande est toujours présente, ajoute Mouhamed Mballo. Selon lui, dans un monde où l’intelligence artificielle prend beaucoup de place, « la différence se situera dans la capacité d’impacter à travers le discours, la plaidoirie. » Lancés depuis plus de dix ans ou récemment dans la formation en art oratoire, en prise de parole en public ou en développement personnel, ces coachs voient en leur métier un domaine prospère qui nécessite cependant un encadrement formel. L’absence d’une certification des coachs aptes à dispenser les enseignements constitue le principal défi auquel la profession fait face actuellement, selon eux. Par Lamine SARR (Stagiaire)

items.title: PPP-PML-N spat continues as Asif's jibe at Bilawal draws 'red line' warning
items.description: In the latest from the ongoing wrangling between the ruling PML-N and its ally in the Centre, the PPP, leaders from the latter have said Defence Minister Khawaja Asif’s remarks directed at Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari were “unacceptable” and crossed the party’s “red line”. The reaction from PPP Senator Sherry Rehman and MNA Sharmila Faruqui on Sunday came on a Nov 19 post by Asif, in which he shared two video clips of PPP Chairperson Bilawal. In the first clip, Bilawal is seen criticising the PTI and its founder, Imran Khan, and in the second one, from his recent address at the Karachi Press Club (KPC), he terms Imran a “political prisoner”. “A person becomes the prime minister and is later imprisoned. So I can either accept that every prime minister in the country’s history has been a thief, or I can accept that all prime ministers in our history have been victims of political revenge,” he adds. Commenting on the two clips, Asif posted on X: “We believed that the new generation would be better and more principled than ours. Did not know they would turn out to be masters of dishonesty and change colours so remarkably.” Reacting to his remarks, Rehman posted on X: “Unacceptable flow of comments from the federal defence minister about the PPP organisation and our leadership, Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari. He has crossed a red line.” Similarly, Faruqui said Asif’s “derogatory language”, particularly his “irresponsible remarks” about Bilawal, were unacceptable for the PPP. “This is a red line for us.” Directly addressing Asif, she went on to say that while everyone had the right to disagree politically, there was a difference between derision and disagreement. “As a senior parliamentarian and a federal minister, you are expected to exercise political judgement, seriousness and decorum. Political differences are addressed through reasoned argument, not personal attacks. Remember, words reflect not only a person’s character but also the dignity of their office.” The PPP and the PML-N have been trading barbs after Bilawal speech at the KPC on Nov 17. On the occasion, the Bhutto scion addressed the ongoing debate on the creation of new provinces, expressed support for several opposition demands and questioned past decisions and actions taken by the ruling coalition. He also warned of bloodshed in Sindh over the creation of new provinces and called for a “political reset”. His remarks drew a strong reaction from senior leaders of the PML-N, Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) and Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan, who accused him of “political hypocrisy”. Asif continued his criticism of Bilawal on Saturday, accusing him of being the “biggest beneficiary and a critic of the system at the same time”. “Rank opportunism,” he commented. Earlier, he brought the ownership of Bilawal House in Lahore into the political argument. In a post on X, the defence minister questioned the ownership and use of Bilawal House, asking: “Can someone disclose the ownership of this property? Who owns it, and who lives there? If this palace-like fortress is being used by anyone, who are they?” The PML-N senior leader further questioned whether those occupying properties without having legal title to them could “morally claim any privileged position”, adding that the 250 million people of Pakistan deserved to know the financial and property details of those who considered high status and privilege their entitlement. Responding to him, PPP senior leader Nadeem Afzal Chan posted a video showing party workers gathering at the Bilawal House in Lahore, saying the property was the home of every PPP worker. “Show us people entering any other big house in the same way. Uncle… answer the questions, whether you like it or not,” Chan said in his X post, directly addressing the defence minister. Separately, the PPP accused the defence minister of attempting to provoke the party into launching personal attacks against the PML-N leadership in retaliation. In a statement posted on X, the PPP said Bilawal had directed party leaders to ignore the defence minister’s remarks and concentrate on issue-based politics. The statement, however, warned that the PPP was also familiar with the political controversies surrounding the PML-N leadership, referring to the Panama Papers, Avenfield properties and Al-Azizia Steel Mills cases. However, even as the heated exchange of words continued between the two sides, President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had decided that all matters would be resolved through dialogue, the Presidency said on Thursday after the two leaders met in Islamabad. The two again met on Saturday to discuss the overall political situation. After the meeting, Rehman urged the government to focus on people’s problems rather than creating new political fault lines. Provocative statements by ministers should be avoided, she said, adding that Bilawal wanted politics to address people’s problems rather than create new divisions. “Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari is looking to prevent bloodshed, not shed it,” she said.

items.title: Washking marks 10 years with over 1,000 sanitation installations
items.description: Washking Limited, a sanitation solutions company, has marked 10 years of operations, having delivered more than 1,000 sanitation installations and reached over 8,000 people. Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Dieudonne Kwame Agudah, disclosed this at the company’s 10th anniversary celebration at Heritage Christian University College, Amasaman, on Friday, November 20, 2026. He said the company, which began with a single toilet construction project, had gradually expanded its operations through reinvestment, referrals, subcontracting and partnerships. Mr Agudah said the company’s early assignments included toilet repairs, desludging and projects linked to the Greater Accra Metropolitan Area (GAMA) sanitation programme, which helped build its capacity and reputation. “Washking did not start with a fleet of vehicles, a boardroom, or large funding. It started with one opportunity: to build one toilet. We did the work. We reinvested what we earned. We used that first opportunity to prepare for the next,” he said. He noted that the company’s growth had been driven by discipline, skills development, integrity and the support of people and institutions willing to create opportunities for emerging businesses. Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Dieudonne Kwame Agudah, According to him, the journey had also been marked by financial pressures, setbacks, operational delays and lessons in trust and people management. Mr Agudah said the company had, over the years, learnt the importance of building strong systems, accountability and institutional structures to sustain its operations beyond the efforts of its founder. He cited earlier impact assessments which estimated that the company’s sanitation interventions had saved nearly 1.4 million hours that people would otherwise have spent travelling to public toilets. The assessments also indicated that more than GH¢329,000 had been earned by artisans and over GH¢737,000 generated in sales for local suppliers, representing more than GH¢1 million in combined local economic activity. The company also reported training 45 people in artisan and sales skills, although Mr Agudah stressed that the figures were from earlier impact reporting and did not represent the company’s cumulative achievements over the full decade. Beyond revenue from its services, he said Washking had mobilised more than $1 million in external funding and support over the past 10 years. He acknowledged the contributions of partners, including Grand Challenges Canada, as well as recognition through the SEED Award and the Empowering People Award. The company also benefited from programmes such as the Toilet Board Coalition Accelerator and UNICEF StartUp Lab. Mr Agudah said the next phase of the company’s development would focus on improving access to sanitation, particularly for lower-income households that struggle to pay for facilities upfront. He said the company was exploring flexible payment arrangements, improved after-sales services and other approaches to make sanitation solutions more financially accessible. “Financial access will remain central, not an afterthought,” he said. He added that Washking was strengthening its management and technical teams, governance structures, operational systems and logistics to improve service delivery. Mr Agudah also called for greater collaboration among government, businesses, development partners and young people to address sanitation challenges in Ghana. He said the sector required the expertise of engineers, technicians, designers, finance specialists, software developers, teachers and community leaders. The company’s vision, he said, was to contribute to a Ghana where children have safe toilets in schools, women and girls have access to privacy and dignity, and households are protected from exposure to human waste and preventable diseases such as cholera. He urged students at the anniversary event to develop their skills, embrace integrity and take advantage of opportunities to contribute to national development. “ The door somebody opened for us must not close behind us. Our first decade proved what one opportunity can begin. Our next decade is about what we can build together,” he said.

items.title: UEW VC urges newly trained teachers to accept postings to deprived communities
items.description: The University of Education, Winneba (UEW) has urged newly trained teachers from Nusrat Jahan College of Education to accept postings to rural and deprived communities to help address educational needs in underserved areas. The call was made by the Dean of the School of Graduate Studies, Professor Awaisu Imurana Braimah, who represented the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Stephen Jobson Mitchual, at the college’s 11th congregation ceremony in Wa on Saturday, November 21, 2026. Addressing the graduands, Prof. Braimah said their professional training should prepare them to serve communities where their skills and expertise were most needed. He urged them not to limit their career aspirations to urban centres but to demonstrate a commitment to national development by accepting postings to underserved communities. “Accept posting to rural or deprived communities where your services are most needed. Remember, service to humanity is service to God,” he said. Prof. Braimah reminded the graduates that they had undergone four years of professional teacher training and were expected to apply the knowledge, skills and competencies acquired to improve the intellectual and moral development of their learners. He said teachers had a critical responsibility to shape the future of children by helping them develop their cognitive, psychomotor and affective abilities to become responsible citizens. He also urged the newly trained teachers to uphold professional ethics, protect the interests of learners and serve as positive role models. “As a newly trained professional teacher, you must be a moral force, and not a moral deviant, a lamp of hope and not an extinguisher of hope for your learners,” he stated. The UEW representative said the graduates had a responsibility to honour the trust parents and guardians placed in teachers by ensuring that learners received the guidance and protection they deserved. Prof. Braimah delivered the address on behalf of the Vice-Chancellor, who was unable to attend the ceremony due to other engagements.

items.title: COP31: New climate deal emerges after overnight negotiations in Turkey
items.description: A new climate agreement has been put forward at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, after negotiations ran into Sunday morning, with the Australian and Turkish presidencies expressing confidence that the proposed package could secure the support of nearly 200 countries. The proposed deal seeks to address some of the most contentious issues at the climate summit, including the future of fossil fuels and financial support for developing countries struggling to adapt to the impacts of climate change. COP31 President Murat Kurum announced the new text during a late-night plenary session, saying the presidencies believed they had found common ground among the negotiating parties. “We believe that we have put forward a text which all the parties can agree upon,” he told delegates. He said negotiators would reconvene later on Sunday morning to begin the process of approving the agreement. The announcement followed days of difficult negotiations that continued beyond the official Friday deadline, through Saturday and into the early hours of Sunday. The latest draft is said to have revised an earlier proposal that attracted criticism from campaigners and some countries for failing to demonstrate sufficient ambition, particularly because it made no reference to ending the use of fossil fuels. Fossil fuels remain one of the most divisive issues in international climate negotiations, with countries holding different positions depending on their economic interests and dependence on oil, gas and coal. Kurum said the latest proposal had addressed concerns surrounding fossil fuels, as well as demands for greater financial assistance to help developing countries prepare for and respond to climate change. The agreement emerged from intensive consultations involving Australia, which is leading the negotiations, Turkey, the host country, and delegations representing nearly 200 nations. The challenge for the two presidencies has been to reach a compromise between countries facing the harshest consequences of global warming and those whose economies depend heavily on producing or consuming fossil fuels. Under the proposed arrangements, delegations were given until 0300 GMT to raise objections, with a further session scheduled for 0600 GMT to begin the approval process. However, whether the package would secure the necessary consensus remained dependent on the response of the negotiating parties. The negotiations have taken place against growing concern about the pace of global warming and the ability of countries to meet the temperature goals agreed under the Paris Agreement. COP31 is the first UN climate summit since the UN’s environmental body confirmed that global temperatures were on course to exceed the 1.5°C threshold that countries committed to pursuing efforts to limit global warming to in the Paris Agreement more than a decade ago. Crossing that threshold would increase the risks and severity of climate impacts, including extreme weather events, placing additional pressure on communities, economies and countries with limited resources to respond. For developing countries, particularly those already experiencing climate-related losses and damage, the outcome of the negotiations could have significant implications for access to climate finance and support for adaptation. The proposed package therefore faces a critical test of whether countries can agree on a common path forward despite their differences over fossil fuels, climate finance and the responsibilities of nations in addressing the climate crisis.

items.title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: NEMA deploys technical team as death toll rises
items.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa The National Emergency Management Agency ,NEMA, said it has deployed a technical team to Bayelsa State to reinforce ongoing search and rescue operations following a boat accident that has now claimed 24 lives and still counting in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities. The boat was conveying passengers from Ayama to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony when it capsized. NEMA in a statement signed by Manzo Ezeki of NEMA Press Unit, said 24 survivors had been rescued, while 24 bodies had been recovered as of Saturday, bringing the number of confirmed fatalities to 24. Search and rescue operations were still ongoing at the time of the announcement. The agency disclosed that 19 of the survivors were taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others, who sustained varying degrees of injuries, were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for medical treatment. The deployment of the technical team followed the earlier activation of NEMA’s South-South Zonal Directorate and the mobilisation of an emergency response team from its Port Harcourt Operations Office to the accident scene. The agency said it is coordinating the rescue operation alongside the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), Nigerian Red Cross Society, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), local divers and other emergency responders. Governor Douye Diri visited the scene of the accident, where he expressed grief over the loss of lives and condoled with the families of the victims. He also commended the emergency agencies, security operatives, local divers and other responders for their intervention and continued efforts to locate possible survivors despite the difficult riverine terrain. NEMA expressed sympathy with the Bayelsa State Government and the families affected by the tragedy, pledging to sustain its collaboration with relevant authorities to coordinate the rescue operation. UEW warns newly trained teachers against sexual relationships with pupils
items.description: The University of Education, Winneba (UEW) has warned newly trained teachers against engaging in sexual relationships with pupils, describing the conduct as reprehensible and unacceptable. The warning was delivered on behalf of the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Stephen Jobson Mitchual, by the Dean of the School of Graduate Studies, Prof. Awaisu Imurana Braimah, at the 11th congregation ceremony of Nusrat Jahan College of Education in the Wa Municipality on Saturday, November 21, 2026. Addressing the graduating teachers, Prof. Braimah said teachers had a responsibility to protect the welfare and interests of learners entrusted to their care by parents and guardians. He cautioned that sexual relationships between teachers and learners could have devastating consequences for the victims and undermine the professional responsibilities of educators. “It is therefore reprehensible and highly unacceptable for teachers to engage in sexual relations with inexperienced learners, which has the potential to ruin their lives forever,” he said. He urged the graduates, who had completed four years of professional teacher training, to uphold high moral standards and apply the knowledge and competencies acquired during their training to positively influence their learners. “As a newly trained professional teacher, you must be a moral force, and not a moral deviant, a lamp of hope and not an extinguisher of hope for your learners,” he stressed. Prof. Braimah said teachers were expected to facilitate the intellectual, moral and practical development of learners, preparing them to become responsible citizens capable of contributing to national development. He further urged the graduates to safeguard the interests of their pupils and demonstrate commitment to their professional responsibilities. The UEW representative also encouraged the newly trained teachers to accept postings to rural and deprived communities, where their services were most needed. “Accept posting to rural or deprived communities where your services are most needed. Remember, service to humanity is service to God,” he said. Prof. Braimah represented the Vice-Chancellor at the ceremony, citing other significant engagements that prevented his physical attendance.
