items.title: Or en baisse, dollar en hausse : les marchés face à de nouvelles turbulences
items.description: La forte baisse des cours de l’or, conjuguée aux lourdes pertes enregistrées sur les marchés boursiers mondiaux, ravive les craintes de turbulences financières susceptibles de dépasser les frontières des États-Unis. Le métal précieux a chuté de plus de 9 % en une semaine, tandis que les Bourses mondiales ont perdu près de 9.000 milliards de dollars de capitalisation par rapport à leurs niveaux records enregistrés en août dernier. Cette situation intervient dans un contexte marqué par des pressions croissantes liées à l’endettement, aux liquidités et aux investissements massifs dans l’intelligence artificielle (IA). Lors des échanges de vendredi, le prix de l’or est tombé à environ 3.502 dollars l’once, avant de se stabiliser autour de 3.534 dollars en fin de séance. Une évolution qui soulève des interrogations sur les raisons du recul de l’un des principaux actifs auxquels les investisseurs ont habituellement recours en période d’incertitude économique. Ces mouvements se sont accompagnés d'une hausse de la demande de dollars américains et d'une pression accrue sur les valeurs technologiques. Cette situation a conduit plusieurs analystes à s'interroger sur l'éventualité d'une crise de liquidités touchant certaines institutions financières, notamment celles qui recourent à l'endettement pour financer leurs positions sur les marchés. Dans une analyse économique publiée sur la plateforme Substack, l'auteure Asha Dubey met en garde contre une interprétation de la baisse de l'or comme un signe automatique d'amélioration de la conjoncture économique. Elle souligne que certaines crises financières s'accompagnent également de ventes d'actifs considérés comme sûrs, lorsque les investisseurs ont davantage besoin de liquidités que de conserver leurs placements. Cette lecture s'appuie sur plusieurs indicateurs, notamment l'augmentation de la dette américaine, la diminution des avoirs de certains grands pays en bons du Trésor américain et l'exposition croissante des institutions financières aux entreprises spécialisées dans l'intelligence artificielle. À cela s'ajoutent les risques liés aux emprunts en yens japonais, autant de facteurs susceptibles d'accroître la vulnérabilité des marchés lorsque plusieurs tensions surviennent simultanément. L'or sous la pression des besoins de liquidités L'or occupe une place particulière sur les marchés financiers en tant qu'actif de couverture contre l'inflation, les fluctuations monétaires et les risques économiques. Toutefois, ce rôle protecteur ne l’empêche pas de perdre de la valeur lorsque les marchés sont confrontés à des vagues généralisées de ventes. Asha Dubey explique que certains fonds d'investissement recourent à l’emprunt pour accroître leurs placements en actions, en obligations et en matières premières. Cette stratégie leur permet de multiplier leurs gains en période de hausse, mais les expose davantage aux pertes lorsque les cours évoluent dans le sens inverse. En cas de forte dépréciation des actifs détenus par ces fonds, les établissements prêteurs peuvent leur demander de fournir des garanties supplémentaires ou de rembourser une partie de leurs engagements. Ils sont alors contraints de vendre rapidement des actifs facilement négociables, y compris de l'or, afin de réunir les liquidités nécessaires. Ces ventes forcées peuvent parfois entraîner la baisse des prix d'investissements dont les fondamentaux économiques n'ont pourtant pas changé. Pour les institutions concernées, la priorité devient alors de réunir les fonds exigés, ce qui pourrait expliquer la concomitance entre le recul de l'or, la baisse des actions et la hausse du dollar. Selon cette analyse, le renforcement de la monnaie américaine en période de turbulences peut également traduire une augmentation de la demande de dollars pour régler les dettes et les transactions financières internationales. Le billet vert conserve en effet une position centrale dans le financement des entreprises, des banques et du commerce mondial. Le mécanisme devient particulièrement préoccupant lorsque les prix chutent suffisamment rapidement pour pousser les investisseurs à fournir davantage de garanties. Les ventes se succèdent alors et les tensions se propagent d'une catégorie d'actifs à une autre, risquant ainsi d'amplifier les pertes sur les marchés. L'auteure ne considère toutefois pas la baisse de l'or comme une preuve définitive de l'existence d'une crise de liquidités. Les cours peuvent également reculer sous l'effet de la hausse des rendements obligataires, du renforcement du dollar ou de prises de bénéfices après des périodes de forte progression. Ces explications restent plausibles tant que ne se manifestent pas d'autres signes de défaillance d'institutions financières ou de difficultés d'accès au financement. Dans les indicateurs qu'elle suit, Asha Dubey évoque également l'évolution des opérations liées à l'or auprès de la Banque des règlements internationaux (BRI). Selon les chiffres qu'elle avance, leur volume est passé d'environ 141 tonnes à la fin du mois d'août à 218 tonnes à la fin du mois d'octobre dernier. Certaines de ces opérations sont liées à l'utilisation de l'or pour obtenir des financements à court terme. Toutefois, leur augmentation ne suffit pas, à elle seule, à démontrer l'existence d'une crise sur les marchés, ni à établir qu'une intervention délibérée aurait été menée pour faire baisser le prix du métal précieux. Dette américaine et risques liés à l'intelligence artificielle Les inquiétudes portent également sur le marché des bons du Trésor américain, qui constitue l'un des piliers du système financier mondial. Le gouvernement américain y recourt pour financer ses dépenses, tandis que les banques, les fonds d'investissement et les institutions internationales les utilisent largement dans leurs opérations financières. Les données du département américain du Trésor citées dans l'analyse font état d'une baisse d'environ 91 milliards de dollars des avoirs cumulés de la Chine et du Japon en bons du Trésor américain durant les mois de juillet et d'août derniers. Le recul total aurait ainsi atteint près de 123 milliards de dollars à la fin du mois de septembre, par rapport aux niveaux enregistrés à la fin du mois de juin. Ces mouvements ne signifient pas nécessairement une perte de confiance dans la capacité des États-Unis à honorer leurs engagements. Ils peuvent également s'expliquer par une réorganisation des réserves, des besoins de liquidités ou des variations de la valeur des actifs. Ils prennent néanmoins une importance particulière dans un contexte où Washington continue de recourir à l’emprunt pour financer son déficit budgétaire. Asha Dubey avertit que l'augmentation des rendements exigés par les investisseurs pour acheter des obligations américaines pourrait renchérir le coût du financement de la dette publique. Cette évolution pourrait également se répercuter sur les taux d'intérêt supportés par les entreprises et les ménages, pesant ainsi sur l'investissement, la consommation et l'activité économique. Parallèlement, le secteur de l'intelligence artificielle est devenu une source croissante de préoccupation pour les institutions financières, après une vague d'investissements massifs dans les centres de données, les processeurs avancés et les infrastructures nécessaires au fonctionnement des modèles numériques. Les entreprises technologiques misent sur des revenus futurs suffisamment importants pour justifier ces dépenses. Toutefois, le financement d'une partie de ces projets par l'endettement les rend plus vulnérables à une hausse des coûts de financement ou à un retard dans la réalisation des recettes commerciales attendues. L'auteure souligne que les risques potentiels dépassent les performances d'une seule entreprise, notamment Nvidia. L'essor de l'intelligence artificielle repose sur un vaste réseau comprenant les fabricants de semi-conducteurs, les exploitants de centres de données, les fournisseurs d'énergie, les banques et les fonds d'investissement. Un ralentissement de la croissance des revenus ou une baisse des valorisations boursières pourrait entraîner des pertes pour les investisseurs et les financeurs, particulièrement lorsque les engagements financiers reposent sur des prévisions très optimistes concernant la demande future de services liés à l'IA. Dans ce contexte, un rapport publié le 13 novembre par la Réserve fédérale américaine indique que 87 % des participants à une enquête sur les risques financiers ont cité l'intelligence artificielle parmi leurs principales sources de préoccupation, contre 50 % lors de la précédente enquête, selon les données reprises dans l'analyse. La Banque centrale européenne a également mis en garde contre les risques liés à l'augmentation des emprunts destinés à financer les projets technologiques avancés, notamment lorsque les dépenses d'investissement dépassent les flux de trésorerie générés par les activités des entreprises. La situation devient d'autant plus sensible que certaines entreprises entretiennent des relations croisées de financement et d'investissement avec leurs fournisseurs et leurs clients. La défaillance d'un projet majeur pourrait ainsi affecter d'autres institutions liées par des contrats, des prêts ou des investissements directs. Le yen japonais et les risques de contagion financière L'un des principaux risques évoqués par Asha Dubey concerne le yen japonais. Depuis plusieurs années, des investisseurs internationaux utilisent cette monnaie pour contracter des emprunts à faible coût, avant de convertir les fonds dans d'autres devises, notamment le dollar, afin de les placer dans des actifs offrant des rendements supérieurs. Cette stratégie repose sur le maintien d'un écart favorable entre les taux d'intérêt et sur la stabilité des taux de change. Elle peut toutefois devenir une source de pertes lorsque le yen s'apprécie brusquement. Le remboursement des emprunts libellés dans la monnaie japonaise devient alors plus coûteux pour les investisseurs qui détiennent des actifs en dollars. Dans une telle situation, les fonds concernés peuvent être contraints de vendre des actions et des obligations pour obtenir les yens nécessaires au remboursement de leurs engagements. Les pressions se transmettent ainsi du marché des changes aux marchés financiers, particulièrement lorsque de nombreux investisseurs ferment simultanément leurs positions. L'auteure souligne également que le Japon fait face à ses propres difficultés, liées aux fluctuations de sa monnaie et à l'augmentation du coût des importations, notamment énergétiques. Les décisions de politique monétaire et les éventuelles interventions sur le marché des changes font ainsi l'objet d'une attention particulière de la part des investisseurs internationaux. Ces risques se combinent à d'autres stratégies reposant sur l'endettement pour acheter des bons du Trésor américain et tirer profit de faibles écarts de rendement. Des variations soudaines des taux obligataires peuvent alors contraindre les fonds d'investissement à réduire leurs positions et à vendre d'importants volumes de titres. Ces scénarios illustrent l'interconnexion croissante des marchés financiers. Une crise de financement touchant un groupe d'institutions peut provoquer une vague de ventes affectant plusieurs catégories d'actifs et différents marchés, avant de se répercuter sur le coût des emprunts, les investissements des entreprises et leur capacité à financer leurs activités économiques. Pour autant, les indicateurs actuels ne fournissent pas suffisamment d'éléments pour conclure à l'imminence d'un effondrement financier mondial. Les bons du Trésor américain ont notamment bénéficié d'une demande de la part des investisseurs en quête de sécurité durant les turbulences de la semaine. Par ailleurs, les évaluations de la Réserve fédérale indiquent que le système bancaire américain dispose toujours de réserves et de capacités financières lui permettant d'absorber les chocs. La différence entre une forte correction des prix et une crise financière généralisée réside notamment dans la capacité des institutions à honorer leurs engagements et à accéder aux liquidités sans être contraintes de procéder à des ventes massives d'actifs. Elle dépend également de l'ampleur de la transmission des pertes des marchés d'investissement vers le système bancaire et l'économie réelle. L'analyse d'Asha Dubey met ainsi en garde contre la convergence de plusieurs facteurs de pression, notamment l'endettement élevé, le recul des valeurs technologiques, les fluctuations monétaires et la hausse de la demande de dollars. Leur combinaison pourrait fragiliser davantage les marchés en cas de nouveau choc, tandis que l'ampleur des conséquences dépendrait du niveau d'exposition des institutions financières et de leur capacité à gérer les risques. En définitive, la chute de plus de 9 % du cours de l'or et les pertes enregistrées sur les marchés boursiers mondiaux justifient un regain de prudence chez les investisseurs. Ces évolutions ne suffisent toutefois pas à annoncer le début d'une crise financière mondiale. La suite dépendra de l'évolution des liquidités, des taux d'intérêt et des performances des entreprises, ainsi que de la capacité des marchés à absorber les vagues de ventes sans basculer dans une période de turbulences financières prolongées. First-Class degree not enough to make excellent teacher – TRCN
items.description: The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) says possessing a first-class degree does not automatically make an individual an excellent teacher. Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, stated this in an interview with Newsmen on Sunday in Abuja. Soyombo stressed the importance of professional competence adding that effective teaching required more than academic qualifications. The registrar explained that teachers must demonstrate competence in five critical areas assessed through the Council’s professional qualifying examination. She identified the areas as basic mathematics, foundational literacy, digital literacy, pedagogy, and safeguarding and child protection. According to her, teachers must possess a sound understanding of basic mathematical concepts to effectively support children’s learning and development. She described foundational literacy as equally important, noting that strong literacy skills enabled teachers to support learning across other subject areas. The registrar said teachers must also understand today’s children, particularly those belonging to the Alpha Generation, and the technological environment in which they operate. She identified digital literacy as the third major area of assessment, describing it as compulsory for teachers seeking to engage effectively with contemporary learners. To illustrate the challenge, Soyombo recalled visiting an examination centre where she encountered an elderly teacher struggling with a computer mouse. “I remember visiting an examination centre recently and meeting an elderly teacher who held a computer mouse and asked me, ‘Madam, what am I going to do with this?’” she said. She said the encounter highlighted the extent of digital literacy challenges confronting some teachers and raised concerns about their preparedness for modern classrooms. “How can teachers effectively engage children in today’s classrooms if they are not comfortable with basic technology?” she asked. Soyombo, however, acknowledged the challenges and disclosed that several training programmes were being implemented to improve teachers’ digital competence. On pedagogy, she said possessing excellent academic qualifications did not automatically translate into the ability to teach effectively. “Having a first-class degree does not automatically make someone an excellent teacher,” she said. She explained that academic qualifications alone could not guarantee that a teacher understood how to apply appropriate instructional methods to address different learning needs. According to her, classrooms comprise learners with varying abilities, including average pupils, children requiring additional support, and gifted and talented learners. She stressed that teachers must possess the pedagogical skills to effectively reach all categories of learners and ensure inclusive classroom experiences. “This is why pedagogy is a critical component of our examination. “Without sound pedagogical skills, a person cannot be considered a fully competent teacher,” she said. The registrar identified safeguarding and child protection as the fifth critical area, emphasising the need to guarantee every child’s safety within the school environment. She said teachers must understand safeguarding principles, child protection requirements and their professional responsibilities towards learners. Soyombo said one positive development was the growing awareness among teachers that preparing for the TRCN examination involved more than simply passing a test. She urged candidates preparing for the next examination scheduled for May, 2027, to explore the Council’s online resources and apply the knowledge gained in their classrooms. “There is no point preparing for the next TRCN examination in May, 2027 without exploring the available resources and ensuring that the knowledge acquired improves children’s learning outcomes,” she said. She emphasised that professional development should translate into measurable improvements in teaching quality and children’s educational experiences. According to her, every agency within the education sector must remain conscious of the learning outcomes it seeks to achieve. “For the education system to progress, every agency must remain conscious of the learning outcomes we want to achieve,” she said. Soyombo maintained that improving professional standards was essential to the credibility and relevance of the Council, insisting that its mandate must produce tangible improvements The post First-Class degree not enough to make excellent teacher – TRCN appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Fire destroys goods worth millions in Yobe market
items.description: …Traders count losses as inferno razes shops in Potiskum By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman A midnight fire outbreak has destroyed several shops and goods worth millions of naira at the Potiskum Central Market in Yobe State, leaving traders counting their losses. The fire, which reportedly started at about 2:00 a.m. on Sunday, November 22, 2026, initially affected the section of the market occupied by traditional medicine dealers before spreading to adjoining shops. The outbreak reportedly caught traders and residents around the market unawares, as the flames spread rapidly through the affected section, making it difficult to salvage goods and other valuables. Following the incident, traders and residents rushed to the scene in an attempt to rescue merchandise and prevent the fire from spreading to other parts of the market. However, several shops and their contents had already been destroyed before effective intervention could be mounted. The arrival of fire service personnel helped contain the inferno and prevent it from spreading to other densely populated sections of the market, thereby averting further destruction. An eyewitness commended the firefighters for their timely intervention, saying their arrival helped prevent the fire from engulfing the entire market. Although no casualties had been reported as of the time of filing this report, the destruction of goods and property has left affected traders facing significant financial losses. The exact number of shops destroyed and the total value of merchandise lost were yet to be ascertained. The Yobe State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA) is expected to assess the affected section to determine the extent of the damage, document the losses suffered by traders and establish the circumstances surrounding the outbreak. The incident has renewed concerns over fire safety in commercial markets, particularly those with closely packed shops and large quantities of combustible materials. For the affected traders, the immediate challenge is how to recover from the losses and rebuild their businesses following the destruction of their merchandise. items.title: Omo-Agege backs Obi, not Tinubu, says aide
items.description: . ..Says APC circulating seven-month-old video to misrepresent senator’s position Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has reaffirmed his support for Peter Obi as the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate for the 2027 general election, dismissing a video circulating on social media in which he expressed support for President Bola Tinubu. Omo-Agege’s position was contained in a statement issued on Saturday by his Special Adviser on Strategy and Communications, Godwin Anaughe, who accused the Delta State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and some officials of the state government of circulating an old video to misrepresent the senator’s political position. The statement said the video, recorded in April 2026 at the Federal Polytechnic, Orogun, when Omo-Agege was still a member of the APC, showed him expressing support for Tinubu. However, Anaughe described the circulation of the footage as misleading, arguing that it predated the senator’s defection from the APC to the NDC in May 2026. According to the statement, Omo-Agege subsequently endorsed Obi at the NDC nomination convention on May 30, 2026, where he seconded the former Anambra State governor’s nomination as the party’s presidential candidate. It added that the senator also declared his support for Obi during an appearance on Arise Television on June 3, 2026, describing him as his preferred presidential candidate for 2027. The aide maintained that Omo-Agege had consistently expressed the same position since joining the NDC. “For the record: Senator Omo-Agege is not endorsing President Tinubu for re-election. He is not going back to the APC. He is the NDC Senatorial candidate for Delta Central, and he stands solidly with Deltans and Nigerians in their resolve to make Peter Obi President in 2027,” the statement said. Anaughe argued that a video recorded while Omo-Agege was still in the APC could not be used to establish his current political allegiance. He accused those circulating the footage of deliberately ignoring the date it was recorded, insisting that the senator’s subsequent public declarations provided a clearer account of his present political position. The statement also challenged the APC to focus on defending its performance in government rather than circulating old political footage. It cited rising food prices, unemployment and declining public confidence as issues Nigerians expected political parties to address. “If the APC wants to talk, it should talk about its record, not its video library,” Anaughe said. He added that Omo-Agege remained focused on the 2027 elections and his support for what he described as a new Nigeria where opportunities would not depend on personal connections. The statement concluded with the slogan, “A New Nigeria Is Possible.” The post Omo-Agege backs Obi, not Tinubu, says aide appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le dirham s'est déprécié de 0,6% face à l'euro
items.description: Le dirham s'est déprécié de 0,6% face à l'euro et de 1,7% vis-à-vis du dollar américain durant la période du 12 au 17 novembre 2026, selon Bank Al-Maghrib (BAM). Au cours de cette période, aucune opération d'adjudication n'a été réalisée sur le marché des changes, indique BAM dans son récent bulletin des indicateurs hebdomadaires. Les avoirs officiels de réserve se sont établis à 512 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) au 13 novembre, en baisse de 0,7% d'une semaine à l'autre et en hausse de 18,4% en glissement annuel. Concernant les interventions de BAM, elles ont totalisé, du 12 au 18 novembre, 153,1 MMDH en moyenne quotidienne. Ce volume se répartit entre des avances à 7 jours pour un montant de 56,9 MMDH, des pensions livrées à plus long terme (46,3 MMDH) et des prêts garantis (50 MMDH). Sur le marché interbancaire, le volume quotidien moyen des échanges s'est situé à 3,5 MMDH et le taux interbancaire s'est établi à 2,25%. Lors de l'appel d'offres du 19 novembre (date de valeur le 19 novembre), la Banque centrale a injecté un montant de 48,7 MMDH sous forme d'avances à 7 jours. Côté Bourse, le MASI a reculé de 1,1% durant la période du 12 au 17 novembre, portant sa contre-performance depuis le début de l'année à -8,6%. Cette évolution reflète notamment des baisses de 5% pour l'indice des « Mines », de 1,4% pour celui des « Bâtiment et matériaux de construction », de 0,5% pour les « Banques » et de 2,1% pour la « Participation et promotion immobilières ». Pour ce qui est du volume des échanges, il est revenu, d'une semaine à l'autre, de 2,9 MMDH à 1,1 MMDH, dont 675,4 millions de dirhams (MDH) réalisés sur le marché central actions et 375,4 MDH au titre de l'introduction en Bourse de Jet Energy. items.title: Full list: FG announces 19 international job vacancies [How to apply]
items.description: The Federal Government, FG has announced 19 international job vacancies for qualified Nigerians at the African Space Agency and the General Secretariat of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC). The vacancies, announced by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, comprise five positions at the African Space Agency headquarters in Cairo, Egypt, and 14 positions at the OIC headquarters in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. The ministry disclosed this in two separate vacancy announcements dated Friday, November 20, 2026, signed by its spokesperson, Oluwafemi Adeniyi, and shared on its official Facebook page on Saturday. According to the ministry, the African Space Agency is recruiting for five positions, with application deadlines of November 25 and December 10, 2026. The positions include Director, Corporate Services (D-1); Director-General, African Space Agency (D-2); Head of Legal Affairs (Grade P-5); Senior Finance Officer (P3); and Senior Human Resources Officer (P3). The ministry said interested and qualified Nigerians should visit the agency’s official website at https://africanspaceagency.org for details of the eligibility requirements and application procedures. For the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the ministry announced 14 vacancies across its departments and specialised units. The positions include Director-General of Political Affairs; Director, Administration Department; Director, Information Department; Director, Conference Department; Director, Muslim Communities and Minorities; Director, African Affairs; and Director, European Affairs and International Organisations. Others are Head of Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officer, Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officers, Administration Department (P2); Director, Peace, Security and Mediation Unit; Chief of HRC Office – IUT; Registrar – IUT; and Deputy Internal Auditor – IUT. The ministry said the application deadlines for the OIC positions range from November 29 to December 24, 2026. It urged interested and qualified Nigerians to visit the organisation’s official vacancy portal at https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies for information on the specific requirements, application procedures and deadlines for each position. How to apply Interested Nigerians can apply through the following official platforms: African Space Agency: Visit https://africanspaceagency.org , navigate to the recruitment or careers section, and check the available positions, eligibility criteria and application instructions. Organisation of Islamic Cooperation: Visit https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies , select the relevant vacancy and follow the stated application procedure. Applicants are advised to review the requirements for their preferred positions and submit their applications before the respective deadlines. items.title: Primature : le Premier ministre Amadou Oury Bah échange avec les responsables de GUI-STAT GROUP
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Amadou Oury Bah, a accordé une audience à une délégation de GuiStat-Group, conduite par son Directeur général, Ibrahima Bah, ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026 à la Primature. Cette rencontre marque une étape déterminante dans le déploiement des activités de ce groupe guinéen spécialisé dans la production de données, les sondages et l’évaluation de la satisfaction des usagers. Au cœur des échanges : la présentation de l’expertise de GuiStat-Group, ses perspectives de développement et les modalités d’un accompagnement institutionnel par le gouvernement. Fort d’un double parcours entre les États-Unis et la Guinée, Ibrahima Bah incarne cette nouvelle génération d’entrepreneurs qui choisissent de revenir sur le continent pour y insuffler un savoir-faire international. GuiStat-Group, dont le nom évoque la donnée et la statistique, se positionne comme un acteur clé dans l’accompagnement des politiques publiques et le développement des affaires. « Mon parcours est à la croisée de deux mondes. J’ai eu la chance de me former et de travailler aux États-Unis, mais mon cœur et mes racines sont ici, en Guinée. J’ai choisi de créer GuiStat-Group parce que je suis convaincu que notre pays regorge d’énormes potentialités, mais qu’il manque parfois d’outils modernes pour les exploiter. Notre mission est d’apporter cette expertise technique, cette rigueur dans la gestion des données et cette vision stratégique pour aider les décideurs et les entreprises à prendre les meilleures décisions », a déclaré le Directeur général face aux médias. La rencontre avec le Premier ministre a été l’occasion pour l’entrepreneur de présenter les axes de développement de sa société. Selon les propos rapportés par le chef du gouvernement, l’État guinéen voit d’un bon œil l’arrivée de tels acteurs. Le Premier ministre Amadou Oury Bah a, au nom de son département, promis un accompagnement conséquent pour GuiStat-Group. Une promesse que le Directeur général a tenu à saluer, soulignant l’importance de ce soutien institutionnel pour une jeune entreprise. « L’accueil du Premier ministre a été extrêmement chaleureux et encourageant. Il a promis, au nom de son département, d’accompagner GuiStat-Group dans son déploiement. C’est une preuve de confiance et un signal fort envoyé à la jeunesse et à la diaspora. Nous ne demandons pas seulement des financements, nous demandons un cadre propice pour travailler, et c’est exactement ce que le gouvernement semble prêt à nous offrir », a-t-il ajouté. « Conakry en mouvement » : un marathon sous le haut patronage présidentiel Au-delà de ses activités statistiques, GuiStat-Group porte un projet d’envergure nationale : « Conakry en mouvement ». Il s’agit d’un marathon de 42,195 km, placé sous le haut patronage de Son Excellence le général Mamadi Doumbouya, président de la République de Guinée. La première édition de cet événement sportif majeur est d’ores et déjà fixée au dimanche 31 janvier 2027. L’objectif affiché est clair : encourager la pratique sportive, fédérer les coureurs et les habitants autour d’une course dans la capitale guinéenne, et faire de Conakry une ville en mouvement. « Ce marathon n’est pas seulement une course. C’est un symbole. Nous voulons faire de Conakry une capitale qui bouge, qui respire, qui rassemble. À travers « Conakry en mouvement », nous invitons chaque Guinéen, chaque habitant, à se dépasser et à partager un moment de sport et de fraternité. Le 31 janvier 2027, nous voulons voir les rues de notre capitale vibrer au rythme des pas des coureurs », a-t-il déclaré avec conviction. Entouré des cadres de son cabinet, le Premier ministre a également formulé plusieurs orientations et suggestions visant à perfectionner les outils de GuiStat-Group, dans l’optique de produire des résultats concrets ayant un impact direct sur les décideurs et les citoyens. À l’issue de la rencontre, les responsables de GuiStat-Group ont salué la qualité de l’accueil réservé par la Primature et assuré de leur détermination à traduire en actes les recommandations du chef du gouvernement. Cette audience ouvre ainsi une nouvelle phase de collaboration entre le groupe et les institutions publiques au service de la performance des services en Guinée.

items.title: APC cancels Cross River campaign kick-off
items.description: …Directs National Assembly, Assembly candidates to continue ward-to-ward campaigns By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Cross River State has cancelled its statewide campaign kick-off scheduled for Thursday, November 26, throwing its campaign timetable for the National Assembly and State House of Assembly elections into temporary uncertainty. The cancellation was announced in a statement issued on Saturday by the Director-General of the Cross River State APC Campaign Council, Prof. Stephen Odey, from the campaign secretariat at 42 Murtala Muhammed Highway, Calabar. The statement said the campaign itinerary, which had earlier been released, had been cancelled, adding that a new date would be announced in due course. The Campaign Council, however, did not disclose the reason for the cancellation. It apologised for any inconvenience the decision might have caused party leaders, stakeholders, candidates, supporters and members of the public. Despite the cancellation, the council directed APC candidates contesting the National Assembly and State House of Assembly elections to continue their grassroots campaign activities. It urged them to proceed with their respective ward-to-ward campaigns, visits, consultations, engagements with stakeholders and other approved campaign activities. The directive suggests that the party intends to sustain grassroots mobilisation while arrangements are being made for a fresh date for the statewide campaign programme. Odey thanked party members and the general public for their understanding and cooperation, assuring them that further information would be communicated in due course. items.title: Dickson mourns victims of Bayelsa boat mishap, seeks safety measures
items.description: Former Governor of Bayelsa State, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, has commiserated with the families and friends of victims of the boat mishap along the Ayama/Oweikorogha waterways in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state. Dickson, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Sunday, described the incident as unfortunate and expressed sadness over the loss of lives. He also extended his condolences to the Bayelsa State Government and the people of the state over the tragedy. The senator said he deliberately scaled down his engagements on Saturday as a mark of respect for those who lost their lives in the incident. According to him, he reduced the number of visitors he attended to and cancelled some previously scheduled visits to reflect on the tragedy. Dickson commended the relevant emergency response agencies and other individuals involved in the rescue operation for their swift response, urging them to sustain their efforts until the operation was successfully concluded. He also called for stricter enforcement of maritime safety regulations and increased public awareness to prevent similar incidents. The former governor stressed the need for continuous safety education for marine operators, security personnel and residents of Bayelsa State. He further urged traditional institutions and the media to support efforts aimed at promoting maritime safety and ensuring compliance with relevant regulations. Dickson reiterated his condolences to the bereaved families, praying that God would grant the deceased eternal rest and give their loved ones the strength to bear the loss. The post Dickson mourns victims of Bayelsa boat mishap, seeks safety measures appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tinubu reiterates commitment to uninterrupted academic calendars
items.description: President Bola Tinubu has reiterated his administration’s commitment to strengthening public tertiary institutions through infrastructure interventions, student financing and policies supporting uninterrupted academic calendars. Tinubu said this during the grand finale of the 37th Convocation ceremony of the Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA) on Saturday in Akure. The ceremony featured conferment of postgraduate degrees on 1,173 graduands and the decoration of the scholars as Professors Emeriti. The President, represented by Prof. Olatunde Ajagbonna of the National Universities Commission (NUC), said his administration recognised universities as vital to scientific, technological and economic progress. “My administration recognises the critical role of universities in national development and has continued to support our tertiary institutions through interventions in infrastructure, equipment, research facilities, laboratories, lecture theatres and student accommodation. “In furtherance of our commitment to student welfare, the Federal Government is also supporting the construction of 1,500-capacity hostel at FUTA in partnership with private sector organisations. “In the education sector, I remain committed to ensuring that no Nigerian student is denied access to tertiary education on account of financial difficulties. “The commitment informed the establishment of Nigerian Education Loan Fund(NELFUND) by my government, which provides financial assistance to eligible students in public tertiary institutions, including support for their upkeep,” he said. Tinubu noted that economic reforms had yielded growth above four per cent in 2026 across oil and non-oil sectors, urging judicious use of federal interventions. He urged the private sector and development partners to collaborate with FUTA in engineering, agriculture, healthcare, artificial intelligence and information technology to drive innovation and job creation. In his goodwill message, Gov. Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State, represented by Commissioner for Education, Science and Technology, Prof. Igbekele Ajibefun, congratulated the graduands and commended the vice-chancellor’s leadership. Aiyedatiwa said the state government would continue to partner with and support FUTA in achieving its aspirations and advancing human capital development. Earlier, FUTA Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Adenike Oladiji, said the event marked the fourth and final convocation of her tenure as the eighth substantive vice-chancellor since May 2022. Oladiji said the university sustained a stable academic calendar and achieved NUC accreditation for its College of Health Sciences. She said FUTA had no abandoned projects, reporting 21 completed projects and 24 ongoing projects, alongside agricultural expansion, a 5,000-layer poultry revamp and a revitalised feed-mill. Giving a breakdown of the 1,173 postgraduate graduands, Oladiji said 641 received Master’s degree and 225 bagged Postgraduate Diploma. She added that 173 earned Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree, 131 graduated from the School of Professional Development, and three received Master of Philosophy (M.Phil) degree. She announced that Prof. Felix Akinyosoye and Prof. Thomas Ofuya would be decorated as Professors Emeriti. Prof. Akinyosoye was decorated as Professor Emeritus of Microbiology, Food Fermentation and Zymology, while Prof. Ofuya was decorated as Professor Emeritus of Crop Entomology. Also speaking, Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council, Dr Olugbenga Awe, congratulated the graduands and the two decorated Professors Emeriti. Awe urged the graduands to approach their future with intellectual humility and apply their knowledge to improve institutions and solve societal challenges. The post Tinubu reiterates commitment to uninterrupted academic calendars appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Photos: Police take over Fountain of Life Church amid leadership crisis
items.description: …As trustees, Jimmy Odukoya trade court actions, church postpones thanksgiving service There was a heavy presence of police personnel at the headquarters of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos, on Sunday, as the leadership crisis rocking the church deepened, leaving worshippers uncertain about who would preside over the regular Sunday service. The security presence came amid a bitter dispute between Senior Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and a group of church trustees over his continued leadership of the ministry founded by his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya. The disagreement has escalated into a legal battle, with both sides seeking judicial intervention over the control and administration of the church. On Friday, Odukoya approached the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his reported removal as senior pastor and questioning the legality of decisions taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees. The suit, instituted by Odukoya alongside the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, named his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church leaders as respondents. The respondents include Pastor Rotimi Okpaise, Pastor Tobi Enuha, Pastor Gbenga Onabanjo, Pastor Fred Ohiani, Pastor Akin Osinbajo, Biodun Balogun and Biodun Awosika. In the court action, Odukoya is challenging the validity of meetings held by some trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, as well as the decisions allegedly taken at those meetings. He is also asking the court to determine whether the trustees could remove him as senior pastor without following the procedures stipulated in the church’s constitution. How the crisis started The leadership dispute became public on November 17 when a group identifying itself as members of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that Odukoya was no longer recognised as the senior pastor, with immediate effect. The trustees reportedly based their decision on a review of the church’s constitution and recorded succession instructions allegedly left by its late founder, Taiwo Odukoya, before his death in 2023. They maintained that the decision was intended to give effect to the founder’s wishes and ensure compliance with the church’s governing provisions. The group subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader pending consultations and the establishment of a substantive leadership structure. However, the announcement immediately generated a counter-reaction from the church, which rejected the purported removal and described it as constitutionally invalid. In a statement issued after the announcement, the church maintained that Jimmy Odukoya remained its duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the Board of Trustees. It argued that his appointment in September 2023 was unanimously approved by the recognised board and that no constitutionally valid decision had been taken to remove him. The disagreement also extended to the control of the church’s communication channels, with the trustees alleging that individuals acting on Odukoya’s behalf had taken control of its official social media accounts without authorisation. Court restrains Odukoya The dispute took another turn on Wednesday, November 18, when the Lagos State High Court granted interim orders restraining Odukoya from holding himself out as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of the church. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin made the orders following an application by the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church. The court also restrained Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with, disrupting or obstructing the church’s governance, administration and activities. The orders were made ex parte, meaning they were granted before Odukoya had an opportunity to respond to the application. However, the court preserved his right to challenge the orders or respond to the substantive claims. The court did not order the closure of the church, suspend its worship services or appoint a replacement for Odukoya. The matter was adjourned until December 1 for mention. Thanksgiving service postponed Amid the unfolding dispute, the church announced the postponement of its much-anticipated 2026 Thanksgiving Service, which had been scheduled for Sunday, November 22. In a notice published on its official social media platforms on Thursday, November 19, the church said a new date would be communicated in due course. The postponement generated further uncertainty among members, particularly as reports circulated that police officers had sealed the church premises and directed workers to vacate the facility. However, the church subsequently dismissed reports that its premises had been sealed. In a message shared on its official social media account on Friday, it declared: “Don’t believe the noise; church is not sealed. See you in church on Sunday.” It also announced that its regular Sunday service would hold at 9am, inviting members to attend physically or participate online. Despite the clarification, a visit to the church premises on Sunday revealed a notable presence of security operatives, while access and activities at the facility appeared restricted. Worshippers were nevertheless seen arriving and being ushered into the main auditorium for the regular service. As of the time of filing this report, it was unclear who would lead the congregation or preside over the service. Vanguard Newspaper The post Photos: Police take over Fountain of Life Church amid leadership crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kankan : le ministre Félix Lamah mise sur les mini-rizeries pour accélérer la révolution rizicole guinéenne
items.description: À l’occasion de l’inauguration d’une unité de transformation de riz de Barka SARL, le ministre de l’Agriculture a annoncé la réalisation de plus de 200 mini-rizeries et un objectif de production annuelle de 5 millions de tonnes de riz dans les cinq prochaines années. Une stratégie destinée à renforcer la transformation locale et à réduire la dépendance de la Guinée aux importations. La Guinée entend accélérer sa marche vers l’autosuffisance en riz. C’est le message porté par le ministre de l’Agriculture, Félix Lamah, à l’occasion de l’inauguration d’une nouvelle unité de transformation de riz de l’entreprise Barka SARL, implantée dans le quartier Dossory, à Kankan. Soutenue par l’État guinéen et la Banque mondiale, à travers le Fonds de développement agricole (FODA) et le Projet de développement de l’agriculture commerciale en Guinée (PEDAG), cette infrastructure s’inscrit dans la volonté des autorités de renforcer les capacités nationales de transformation et de promouvoir l’investissement privé dans le secteur agricole. Dans son allocution, le ministre s’est réjoui de la mise en service de cette unité industrielle, qui a bénéficié d’un financement d’un milliard de francs guinéens du FODA et d’un appui avoisinant 300 000 dollars du PEDAG. Avec une capacité de transformation de 10 tonnes de riz par jour, soit environ 3 800 tonnes par an, la rizerie dispose d’équipements permettant d’assurer plusieurs opérations, notamment le stockage, le nettoyage, le décorticage et l’étuvage du riz local. Pour Félix Lamah, cette réalisation traduit une évolution dans la conception de la politique agricole nationale, avec une place davantage accordée au secteur privé. « Ce qui se réalise ici est le début d’un changement de paradigme », a-t-il déclaré, avant de préciser le nouveau rôle attendu de l’État : « L’État ne doit plus être celui qui contrôle tout, qui produit tout, qui transforme tout. Il doit plutôt être celui qui encadre, qui accompagne, qui subventionne lorsque c’est nécessaire et qui apporte des conseils et du financement à travers ses partenaires. » Cette orientation vise notamment à faire des petites et moyennes entreprises agricoles des acteurs majeurs du développement des chaînes de valeur, en complémentarité avec les pouvoirs publics. Plus de 200 mini-rizeries et 5 millions de tonnes de riz en perspective Au-delà de l’inauguration de l’unité de Barka SARL, Félix Lamah a présenté les ambitions du gouvernement pour la filière rizicole. Dans le cadre de la stratégie nationale de développement de cette filière, le ministère prévoit la réalisation de plus de 200 mini-rizeries dans les principaux bassins de production du pays. L’objectif affiché est d’atteindre une production annuelle de 5 millions de tonnes de riz au cours des cinq prochaines années. Le ministre a, par ailleurs, rappelé le paradoxe d’un pays disposant d’importantes ressources agricoles, mais qui continue de recourir aux importations pour couvrir une partie de ses besoins alimentaires. Selon les chiffres qu’il a avancés, la Guinée a importé environ un million de tonnes de riz en 2025. « Nous avons 13 millions d’hectares de terres arables, une pluviométrie où il pleut en moyenne six mois dans l’année et une jeunesse. Alors, il faut que nous puissions travailler notre terre et consommer ce que nous produisons sur nos propres terres », a-t-il insisté. Dans cette perspective, le programme Simandou 2040 prévoit notamment l’aménagement de 150 000 hectares consacrés à la riziculture. Les investissements annoncés devraient porter sur la mécanisation, l’irrigation et le désenclavement des bassins de production. Le ministre a également évoqué la deuxième phase du Projet de développement de l’agriculture commerciale, conduite en partenariat avec la Banque mondiale. Celle-ci prévoit de renforcer les chaînes de valeur du riz, du fonio et de l’aviculture, avec pour ambition de contribuer à l’autosuffisance alimentaire et nutritionnelle. Barka SARL ambitionne d’exploiter 427 hectares Prenant la parole, le directeur général de Barka SARL, Mohamed Kaba, a expliqué les raisons ayant motivé l’implantation de l’unité industrielle à Kankan. Il a notamment mis en avant la proximité des zones de production et le potentiel agricole de la région, qui facilitent l’approvisionnement de l’usine en matières premières. « Kankan a un potentiel majeur. Kankan est proche des agriculteurs de riz, ce qui facilite le transport des matières premières et permet de produire en grande quantité. C’est la raison pour laquelle nous avons décidé d’installer notre usine à Kankan », a-t-il expliqué. L’entreprise dispose également d’une plaine agricole de 427 hectares, dont 250 hectares ont déjà été exploités cette année. La direction entend progressivement mettre en valeur toute cette superficie. « Aujourd’hui, nous avons une plaine de 427 hectares. Nous sommes très heureux que cette année, nous ayons réussi à faire 250 hectares. L’année prochaine, nous voulons augmenter jusqu’à exploiter entièrement les 427 hectares », a annoncé Mohamed Kaba. Le responsable de Barka SARL a salué l’accompagnement des autorités guinéennes, notamment à travers le FODA et le PEDAG. Ces dispositifs ont contribué au financement des activités agricoles, à la finalisation de l’usine et à la réalisation des infrastructures de stockage. Il a également souligné l’importance des partenariats privés dans le développement de l’entreprise, tout en réitérant sa reconnaissance aux autorités pour leur soutien à la valorisation du secteur agricole. Les producteurs espèrent doubler leurs superficies cultivées Du côté des producteurs, l’installation de cette unité de transformation à proximité des zones de production suscite des attentes importantes. Pour Mamoudou Touré, agriculteur, cette infrastructure constitue une opportunité de développer les exploitations rizicoles et d'accroître les volumes de production. « Nous sommes vraiment contents de l’inauguration de cette usine. Nous remercions les initiateurs. Elle va nous permettre d’accroître notre production locale. Si nous avions l’habitude de produire sur 100 hectares, nous allons augmenter à 200 hectares, parce que nous ne craignons plus les difficultés liées à la transformation : elle se fait désormais ici, chez nous », s’est-il réjoui. Pour les producteurs, la proximité d’une unité industrielle représente ainsi une possibilité de réduire les contraintes liées à la transformation du riz et de mieux valoriser les récoltes. Elle pourrait également favoriser l’extension des superficies cultivées, à condition que les capacités de collecte et de transformation répondent aux volumes produits. Le ministère promet un accompagnement technique À cette occasion, Félix Lamah a encouragé la direction générale de Barka SARL à multiplier les investissements de ce type. Il a également réaffirmé la disponibilité de son département à apporter un accompagnement technique à l’entreprise. Cet appui devrait notamment mobiliser l’Institut de recherche agronomique de Guinée (IRAG), la Direction nationale de l’agriculture et les structures chargées du conseil agricole. Les interventions envisagées concernent notamment l’accès aux semences de qualité, l’amélioration des pratiques culturales ainsi que l’organisation des producteurs en groupements et en coopératives. L'un des enjeux est de garantir un approvisionnement régulier de la rizerie en riz paddy, indispensable à la rentabilité et à la pérennité de l'investissement. À Kankan, cette inauguration marque ainsi une nouvelle étape dans les ambitions de développement de la filière rizicole guinéenne. Entre investissements privés, accompagnement public, extension des superficies cultivées et multiplication des unités de transformation, le gouvernement entend construire une chaîne de valeur capable de mieux répondre à la demande nationale. Reste désormais à traduire ces ambitions en résultats concrets, notamment en matière d'augmentation durable de la production, de maîtrise des coûts de transformation et de réduction effective des importations de riz. Karifa Kansan Doumbouya L’article Kankan : le ministre Félix Lamah mise sur les mini-rizeries pour accélérer la révolution rizicole guinéenne est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: “Ibrahima Sory Keïta, dit Petit Sory : une légende du football guinéen s’en va” – Fodé Oussou se souvient de son ami
items.description: C’est avec une profonde tristesse que j’ai appris le décès de mon grand frère Ibrahima Sory Keita, affectueusement appelé Petit Sory, ancienne gloire du mythique Hafia 77 et figure emblématique du football guinéen. J’ai eu le privilège de côtoyer Petit Sory lorsqu’il résidait à Landréah, dans la commune de Dixinn. C’est d’ailleurs dans la concession de la famille Yansané, au même endroit, que j’avais construit ma pharmacie. Je garde de lui le souvenir d’un homme profondément humble, courtois, gentil et accessible. Nous passions parfois de longues heures à échanger, notamment sur le Hafia Football Club, ses exploits et les grandes figures du football africain de son époque. Au-delà du champion, j’ai découvert un homme d’une grande simplicité, dont la gentillesse et la disponibilité m’ont profondément marqué. Je suis également fier d’avoir eu l’occasion, en ma qualité de président du groupe parlementaire des Libéraux Démocrates, de prendre la parole à l’hémicycle pour plaider en faveur d’un traitement digne et d’une reconnaissance nationale à l’endroit des anciens footballeurs du Hafia Club, en hommage aux immenses services qu’ils ont rendus à notre Nation. Je souhaitais que ces hommes soient honorés de leur vivant, à la hauteur de leur contribution à la gloire de la Guinée. Petit Sory était présent dans la salle ce jour-là. À l’issue de mon intervention, il était venu me remercier chaleureusement. C’est à cette occasion que nous avons pris la photo que je partage aujourd’hui, avec beaucoup d’émotion, en souvenir de ce moment. Aujourd’hui, cette image prend une dimension toute particulière. Elle témoigne d’une rencontre, d’une estime réciproque et d’un souvenir que je garderai précieusement. À sa famille, à ses proches, à ses anciens coéquipiers et compagnons du Hafia Club, aux anciennes gloires du Syli National ainsi qu’à l’ensemble du peuple de Guinée, j’adresse mes sincères et profondes condoléances. Que le Tout-Puissant Allah lui accorde Son infinie miséricorde, lui pardonne ses péchés et l’accueille dans Son vaste Paradis. Repose en paix, mon cher grand frère Petit Sory. La Guinée n’oubliera jamais ce que tu as apporté à son football et à son rayonnement. items.title: SERAP sues NDPC, INEC over alleged AI manipulation of voters’ register
items.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has filed a lawsuit against the National Data Protection Commission (NDPC) and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) over “the alleged use by some INEC officials of AI-generated photographs to manipulate INEC’s preliminary Register of Voters, and the failure to ensure the protection of voters’ personal data and investigate the alleged violations.” The lawsuit follows INEC’s acknowledgement of suspected AI-generated photographs and questionable records in the preliminary Register of Voters. On 1 November 2026, INEC reportedly disclosed that its Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) had flagged 268 records for review, with some individuals allegedly exploiting official registration credentials. In suit number FHC/ABJ/CS/2863/2026, filed last week at the Federal High Court in Abuja, SERAP is seeking “an order of mandamus to direct and compel the NDPC to make an independent and reasoned determination on the allegations of suspected AI-generated photographs, alterations to personal data and unverifiable records in INEC’s preliminary Register of Voters, including whether to initiate an investigation.” SERAP is also seeking “an order of mandamus to direct and compel the NDPC to obtain and examine relevant records, documents and electronic data held by INEC to establish the nature and extent of the reported irregularities and determine whether the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 has been violated.” SERAP is further seeking “an order of mandamus to direct and compel the NDPC to exercise its enforcement powers under the Act, including issuing corrective orders, imposing appropriate fines and sanctions, and facilitating remedies or compensation for voters affected by any established violations.” In the suit, SERAP is arguing that: “The alleged irregularities raise serious concerns about the security and integrity of Nigerians’ personal data and the reliability of the voters’ register ahead of the 2027 general elections.” SERAP is also arguing that: “The security and accuracy of the voters’ register are fundamental to the protection of Nigerians’ personal data and their right to participate in public affairs. Nigerians should not have to worry that their personal information could be altered, manipulated or accessed without proper safeguards.” SERAP is further arguing that: “INEC’s acknowledgement of questionable records and suspected AI-generated photographs makes an independent investigation particularly important. The public needs to know what happened, whether the law was breached and what measures are being taken to prevent a recurrence.” According to SERAP, “The NDPC should exercise its statutory powers independently and without delay. Any investigation must establish the facts, protect affected voters and ensure that those responsible for any unlawful conduct are held accountable.” The lawsuit, filed on behalf of SERAP by its lawyers, Oluwakemi Agunbiade, Kehinde Oyewumi, Andrew Nwankwo, and Valentina Adegoke, reads in part: “The investigation should establish the nature and extent of the reported irregularities, including the number and geographical distribution of affected records, when and how they were created or altered, and the persons or institutions responsible.” “The introduction of questionable records, including photographs suspected to have been artificially generated, raises legitimate concerns about the accuracy and reliability of the register and the safeguards protecting its integrity.” “The reported irregularities may involve the unlawful alteration or processing of personal data, possible misuse of authorised access credentials and failures to ensure the accuracy, integrity and security of personal data held and processed by INEC.” “The court should direct and compel the NDPC to conduct an independent forensic examination of the affected database and systems to determine whether personal data were unlawfully accessed or altered and whether INEC complied with the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023.” “The court should also direct and compel the NDPC to determine whether the incidents constitute a personal data breach under section 65 of the Act and whether INEC has complied with its applicable notification and record-keeping obligations.” “According to INEC’s statement of 27 October 2026, the Commission acknowledged public concerns regarding ‘suspected AI-generated photographs appearing in the Preliminary Register of Voters’ published on its website.” “INEC stated that, during the physical display of the register nationwide from 9 to 15 October 2026, ‘a number of questionable registration records were identified and flagged for further examination’. The Commission said it had commenced a review and was taking ‘appropriate corrective action’.” “INEC also acknowledged that the online publication ‘does not reflect all ongoing data-cleanup activities’ and that it was ‘examining the circumstances surrounding the suspicious photographs, including possible technical or procedural lapses’.” “INEC stated that the preliminary register was not the final certified register and undertook to complete the necessary verification, adjudication and data-cleanup processes before certifying the final Register of Voters on 15 December 2026.” “INEC has reportedly acknowledged the existence of questionable voter-registration records and indicated that some registration officers may have used their official access credentials to introduce irregular records, including photographs suspected to have been generated using artificial intelligence.” “While the Commission has indicated that it is reviewing the matter, an independent investigation by the NDPC is necessary to establish the full circumstances, determine the extent of the irregularities and ensure accountability.” “An internal review by INEC cannot substitute for the NDPC’s independent exercise of its statutory data-protection mandate.” “The reported irregularities in INEC’s voter-registration database are particularly concerning because the database contains the personal data of millions of Nigerians and is fundamental to the exercise of their constitutional and democratic rights.” “Any unlawful alteration, manipulation or compromise of this information could undermine public confidence in the electoral process, compromise the accuracy and reliability of the voters’ register, and expose eligible voters to the risk of wrongful exclusion.” “The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 gives the NDPC clear powers to investigate possible violations, obtain relevant information and documents, and require compliance by data controllers and processors. Sections 24 and 39 of the Act require personal data to be processed accurately and securely, and protected against unlawful alteration, loss or unauthorised access.” “Section 65 of the Act defines a personal data breach to include a breach of security leading, or likely to lead, to the unlawful alteration, loss, unauthorised disclosure of or access to personal data.” “Under section 40, data controllers must notify the NDPC of a breach likely to pose a risk to individuals’ rights and freedoms within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, and communicate the breach to affected individuals where it is likely to result in a high risk. The Act also requires the maintenance of records of personal data breaches.” “The reported involvement of registration officers with authorised access to the database makes it particularly important to establish whether adequate safeguards were in place and whether those safeguards were circumvented or misused. The use of authorised credentials does not, by itself, establish that subsequent access or processing was lawful or within the scope of the officer’s authority.” “The reported irregularities also raise concerns about Nigerians’ constitutional and international human rights, including the rights to privacy and political participation.” “Section 37 of the Nigerian Constitution 1999 (as amended) guarantees the right to privacy. Article 13 of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights and Article 25 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights protect citizens’ rights to participate freely in government and to vote in genuine elections.” “These rights require effective safeguards to ensure that eligible voters are not arbitrarily prevented from exercising their political rights.” “The integrity and accuracy of the Register of Voters are indispensable to the effective exercise of the rights to participate in public affairs and to vote in genuine elections. The reported irregularities must be treated with the seriousness they deserve.” “INEC has indicated that it will complete the necessary verification and data-cleanup exercises before certification of the final Register of Voters. It is therefore essential that the reported irregularities are promptly and independently investigated and effectively addressed before the register is finalised.” “Nigerians must be able to trust that the register on which the 2027 general elections will be conducted is accurate, reliable and adequately protected against manipulation.” “The protection of personal data, the integrity of electoral institutions and the effective exercise of political rights are mutually reinforcing obligations under the Nigerian Constitution and international human rights law.” “Addressing the reported irregularities transparently and effectively would strengthen public confidence in the electoral process and safeguard Nigerians’ right to participate freely in public affairs.” No date has been fixed for the hearing of the suit. The post SERAP sues NDPC, INEC over alleged AI manipulation of voters’ register appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kaduna Clerics, monarchs unite to keep girls in school, support young mothers
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Faith and traditional leaders in Kaduna State have pledged to collaborate with the Brain Builders Youth Development Initiative (BBYDI) to tackle barriers to girls’ education and facilitate the return of married girls, teenage mothers and those forced out of school by financial difficulties. The commitment was made at the inauguration of the Coalition of Faith and Traditional Leaders for Girls’ Education, organised by BBYDI under its Faith and Tradition for Girls’ Education Project, with support from the Malala Fund, at Asa Pyramid Hotel, Kaduna. At the event, the organisation also unveiled an advocacy toolkit, including a local-language edition, a coalition charter and terms of reference to guide religious and traditional leaders in promoting girls’ education across communities. The toolkit is designed to help religious and traditional leaders use sermons, congregational gatherings, traditional council meetings and community dialogues to sensitise parents and guardians on the importance of keeping their daughters in school. The initiative is also expected to address challenges such as child marriage, poverty, insecurity and the stigma confronting girls who become pregnant or have children while still of school age. Speaking at the inauguration, BBYDI Programme Director, Halimat Olufade, said consultations with faith and traditional leaders across the project’s 12 local government areas informed the formation of the coalition and the development of the advocacy materials. She disclosed that the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) and Jama’atu Nasril Islam (JNI) had expressed willingness to deploy their churches, mosques and community platforms to encourage families to prioritise girls’ education. According to her, particular attention would be given to married girls and young mothers who wish to return to school, stressing that marriage or motherhood should not permanently deprive girls of educational opportunities. “No girl should have to abandon her education because she becomes a wife or a mother. No girl’s circumstances should permanently close the doors to learning,” Olufade said. Governor Uba Sani, who commended BBYDI for the initiative, pledged the state government’s support and partnership. The governor, represented by Mallam Abass Shehu, said the administration had provided conditional cash transfers to 46,572 girls to improve school attendance, retention and completion. He added that the government had also constructed and renovated schools through the Adolescent Girls Initiative for Learning and Empowerment (AGILE) and the Reaching Out-of-School Children project. Similarly, the Commissioner for Education, Abubakar Sani Sambo, commended the organisation and expressed the ministry’s readiness to work with the coalition. Sambo urged members to use their influence to encourage parents to enrol their daughters in school, support their continued education and challenge cultural practices that undermine girls’ access to learning. He also stressed the need to address the educational challenges facing girls with disabilities and those whose social circumstances make school attendance difficult. The Emir of Zazzau, Ahmad Nuhu Bamalli, represented by the Makaman Malaman Zazzau, Sani Yusuf Magaji, also expressed support for the initiative, saying the emirate was willing to collaborate with BBYDI and other organisations on practical measures to expand girls’ access to education. Magaji recalled historical efforts by the Zazzau Emirate to promote girls’ education, noting that a former emir, Jafaru Dan Isyaku, dedicated Babban Dodo Primary School as a girls’ boarding school and enrolled his daughter, Hajiya Talle. He said district heads, ward heads and officials of the then Zaria Native Authority were also encouraged to enrol their daughters in primary schools. In her remarks, the Director of the Gender Policy Unit at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, Rahanatu Lawal, urged the coalition to involve girls and young women in designing programmes and policies affecting their education. She said girls should be given opportunities to articulate the challenges they face, particularly regarding school safety, retention and the support required to return to classrooms after dropping out. Olufade said the coalition’s success would ultimately be determined by measurable improvements in girls’ education, including increased school retention and the number of girls who return to school and complete their education. The post Kaduna Clerics, monarchs unite to keep girls in school, support young mothers appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: PSG star Doue in tears after suffering worrying knee injury against Nice
items.description: Paris Saint-Germain star Desire Doue was stretchered off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as the reigning French and European champions beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1 on Saturday. Doue went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead. He looked in agony as he clutched his right knee, and the match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doue to receive treatment before being carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium. PSG will now be dreading discovering the extent of the injury, having lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month. The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doue looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too. “We will need to wait until tomorrow for the test results, but it is obviously a serious injury,” PSG coach Luis Enrique told broadcaster Ligue 1+. The 21-year-old French international, who can play on the wing or in midfield, has been arguably PSG’s best player this season after playing a key role in their Champions League triumphs in each of the last two campaigns. He has notably scored three goals in three Champions League appearances this season for PSG, who sold Bradley Barcola to Liverpool at the beginning of the campaign and have seen Ousmane Dembele struggle with his fitness recently. – ‘Not a problem’ – “This is the life of a professional player at the very highest level,” added Luis Enrique. “You just have to accept it and I am sure he will find a way to recover well and come back even stronger.” Asked about the possibility of moving to sign a replacement in the January transfer window, the Spanish coach said PSG were “always open to possibilities”. “We have players who can come in and we will overcome this as a team. It is not a problem,” he added. Earlier, Algerian international Mohamed Amoura had given Nice the lead only for Senny Mayulu to equalise with a penalty awarded after a VAR check following a handball in the home box. Doue — who was wearing a mouthguard after one of his teeth became dislodged while playing for France against Italy during the international break — put PSG ahead a minute after that goal, turning in at the back post from an Achraf Hakimi assist for his sixth of the season in all competitions. His replacement Ferran Torres scored PSG’s third in the 85th minute, controlling in the box before finishing on the turn for his eighth goal of the season — but first in two months. Ali Abdi pulled one back for Nice in stoppage time, but their run of three straight wins was ended as PSG made it 12 victories on the bounce. Eight of those wins have come in Ligue 1, in which PSG are now five points clear at the top from Lille, who lost 1-0 at home to Lyon with Mads Bidstrup scoring the only goal. Paris FC now have the chance to climb into second place and close the gap to PSG to three points by beating Angers on Sunday. Lyon are up to fourth, while Brest moved into the top six after winning 1-0 at Strasbourg, as the home side lost in their first game since appointing Portugal’s Vitor Matos of Swansea City as coach. Monaco needed a late Edan Diop equaliser to draw 1-1 at home to Auxerre as their winless run in Ligue 1 stretched to six games. Lens drew 1-1 with Toulouse in their first match under new coach Didier Digard. The post PSG star Doue in tears after suffering worrying knee injury against Nice appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: COP31 faces collapse threat as latest draft fails to mention fossil fuels
items.description: The COP31 presidency proposed an eleventh-hour deal Sunday that again fails to mention fossil fuels — an omission that deepened a tense standoff at the UN climate talks. The latest offering by summit co-hosts Turkey and Australia published deep into overtime leaves unresolved tensions over planet-heating fossil fuels but retains a much-sought goal to electrify the global economy. The proposal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations at a closing session Sunday but they have struggled to bridge differences during two weeks of grinding negotiations. The European Union and other nations have pushed for strong language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, a call that has faced resistance from oil-rich Saudi Arabia. An EU official told AFP the latest proposal was a “backwards” step, warning there was a “very real possibility” that COP31 ends with no deal. “I am more pessimistic today than I was yesterday,” the official said on condition of anonymity. “The situation is difficult, and the outcome is uncertain. The oil-producing countries are putting up a fierce fight,” a German official said. A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP. Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks and the summit comes against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran. A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase out of fossil fuels but a second, pared-down version released Thursday stripped away all mentions of coal, oil and gas. Threats of a walkout prompted Turkey and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the European Union and Saudi Arabia in a bid to broker a compromise. The latest text introduces a reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels — but stops short of naming them explicitly. And it retains a contentious push to expand carbon capture and storage, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions. “We are very disappointed with how the text looks,” the environment minister of Antigua and Barbuda, Michael Joseph, told AFP after leaving the COP31 presidency’s offices. “I can’t honestly say that I’m okay with it passing” in its current state, Joseph said, adding that the draft was “quite silent” on fossil fuels. – Goal to electrify – The draft also calls for global efforts to boost the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035 and the expansion of “clean energy”. The summit had been under pressure to show progress in tackling soaring greenhouse gas emissions in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia. Facing blowback over fossil fuels, Turkey and Australia pointed to “electrification” as a way to cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security. This works by replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels directly — like diesel cars and gas heating — with electric alternatives. But some nations had demanded an explicitly “clean” target to ensure the electrification push was powered by renewable energy and not fossil fuels. Around one-third of global electricity is produced using coal and another fifth using fossil gas. Attempts by Saudi Arabia, India and Kenya meanwhile to delay the next set of reports by the UN’s Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) have been another major source of friction at the talks. The draft text “highlights the importance” of these reports for an upcoming stocktake of global carbon-cutting efforts in 2028. Dozens of countries across Europe, Africa and the Pacific want these assessments by the global scientific authority on climate change published in time for that crucial stocktake. Countries have also disagreed at COP31 over how to respond to the looming breach of the 1.5C warming target set under the Paris climate accord. The latest draft expressed “deep concern” that global warming would cross 1.5C above pre-industrial levels in the next few years. The talks also jammed over long-running complaints that rich nations are shirking their obligations to help developing nations confront climate change. The removal of a $120 billion target for climate adaptation angered developing nations.
